【協賛企業紹介⑤】
JSFはたくさんの協賛企業様からご協賛をいただいております。
以下にて企業様をご紹介させていただきます。

・日研フード株式会社（五感で味わう青みかん）
捨てられてしまう「青みかん」をアップサイクルし、独自技術で原料化。おいしく飲めて体に良い粉末飲料として提供しています。当日は青みかんドリンクの試飲ブースと、青みかん香るサウナを出展します。

・フォージバンド株式会社
人事・組織コンサルティングとSES事業を展開。採用・育成・定着や組織づくりなど、企業ごとに異なる人事・組織課題の解決を支援しています。

・株式会社グレイスヴィジョン

川崎市高津区にあるデジタルサイネージ会社。サイネージ選びから施工、コンテンツ制作、導入後のメンテナンスまでワンストップでサポート。可動式LEDサイネージのレンタルも行っています。

・ひかり味噌株式会社
@hikarimiso 
1936年創業、長野県発の味噌メーカー。「自然の恵み、いただきます。」をコンセプトに、無添加味噌やオーガニック味噌、即席みそ汁、スープ、塩こうじ、甘酒などを展開。当日は甘酒「晴れのち糀」のサンプリング出店を行います。

・株式会社Kooga（SAUNA NAYA）
@sauna_naya 
茨城県古河市を拠点に、映像・写真制作、SNS運用、Web制作、イベント企画運営などを手がけるクリエイティブカンパニー。「JAPAN TEA EXPO」の企画運営やサウナ施設「SAUNA NAYA」も運営しています。当日は世界一に選ばれたお茶サウナ「SAUNA NAYA」を出展します。

・BUGGY STORY（バギーストーリー）
@buggystory 
千葉・勝浦の森と海を舞台に、絵本の主人公になって冒険するアトラクション型サウナ「BUGGY STORY」。森でハーブを摘み、香りを楽しむサウナや、バギーで森を駆け抜けて海へ向かう体験など、物語とリアルを融合したネイチャーファンタジー体験を提供します。当日はコラボテントサウナの出展に加え、物語の絵本も紹介します。

caption:
【協賛企業紹介③】
JSFはたくさんの協賛企業様のご協賛をいただいております。
以下にて企業様をご紹介させていただきます。

・Sauna Camp
@saunacamp 
テントサウナ「MORZH」の販売などを手がけるテントサウナ専門店。アウトドアサウナの楽しみ方を発信し続けるパイオニアです。

・エイケン工業株式会社
@eiken_kk.co.jp 
静岡・御前崎の自動車部品メーカー。培ってきたものづくり技術を活かし、テント型サウナ「ガレージサウナ」を開発・展開しています。

・AMBER
@amber_official_totonoi 
北欧の熱と和の蒸気を融合したテントサウナブランド。羽釜から沸き出る圧倒的な蒸気に包まれる「羽釜蒸気浴」を提案しています。当日は大型ドームテントからミニテントまで、AMBERのテントを体感できます。

・iSAUNA
@isauna_official 
「そうだ、サウナ呼ぼう。」でお馴染みの出張テントサウナサービス。自宅や別荘、キャンプ場、野外イベントなど、日本全国にテントサウナを届けています。

・株式会社池光エンタープライズ（kiyasume）
@kiyasume_ikemitsu 
「気が休まればそれでいい」をコンセプトにしたリラクゼーションドリンク。アルコールフリー・ノンカフェインで、ゆずの爽やかな香りと飲みやすい微炭酸が特徴です。

・CHILL DOG
@chilldog_sauna 
サウナが好きすぎて仕事を辞め、テントサウナで日本一周していたサウナー集団。全国47都道府県・約4,000人とサウナイベントを実施してきました。現在は富士山麓・富士宮市を拠点に、サウナ施設のオープンを準備しています。

・一般社団法人全国サ飯協会
@sameshi_jp 
サウナ後の食事「サ飯」の文化を広める団体。ととのった後の美味しい一皿で、サウナ体験の締めくくりを提案しています。

・頂マーラータン
@maratan_tokyo 
もちもちの太生春雨と特製スープが自慢のマーラータン専門店。発汗を促す薬膳スープを提供し、サウナとの相性が良いサ飯を楽しめます。

・キンコーズ川崎駅前
ポスターやパンフレットなどのオンデマンド印刷サービスを提供。川崎駅前店として、イベントを支える印刷物づくりをサポートしています。

・Mahārāja
@maharaja__ritual 
インド政府認定アーユルヴェーダセラピストが属するサウナ団体。全国の温浴施設や薬草ハーブサウナのプロデュースをはじめ、農薬不使用の業務用薬草ハーブの生産・管理・収穫・調合まで行っています。

・リトルリンク株式会社
クラウドファンディングの実行支援を行う会社。商品販売・イベント・資金調達など幅広いジャンルをサポートし、JAPAN SAUNA FESTIVALのプロジェクト推進を支えています。

・セントウボウズ（株式会社BUL DE BOIN）
@sentoubozu 
大阪発の銭湯クリエイティブ。古き良き街の銭湯カルチャーを未来へ残すことを目指し、銭湯をより面白く、クリエイティブに発信しています。スタッフTシャツのコラボも担当しています。

・TENTSAUNA BASE
@uryu_tentsaunabase 
「あなただけのサウナ体験を、どこへでも」を掲げる出張テントサウナの企画・運営会社。JAPAN SAUNA FESTIVAL 2026の副実行委員長も務めています。

caption:
【協賛企業紹介②】
JSFはたくさんの協賛企業様からご協賛をいただいております。
以下にて企業様をご紹介させていただきます。

・SOLA WEATHER CARE
@sola_official_jp 

どんな天気でも芯から輝く晴れツヤ髪へ導く、全天候型ウェザーケア ヘアケアブランド。ヒートケア成分*が熱から髪を守り補修するので、サウナーさんにもおすすめ！ *レブリン酸（保護）

・素数株式会社（NOSEMINT）
@sosu_jp_official 
独自ブレンドの“衝撃ミント”で、嗅ぐだけ爽快リフレッシュ。鼻からスーッと抜ける清涼感は、サウナとの相性も抜群。NOSEMINTサウナでは、ミント香る特別な爽快体験をお楽しみいただけます。

・伊良コーラ株式会社
@iyoshicola 
イヨシコーラは、スパイスと柑橘の香りが弾ける唯一無二のコーラです。サウナ後の火照った身体と乾いた喉に、きめ細かな炭酸、爽やかな酸味、奥行きのあるスパイス感がすっと染み込み、深くととのう余韻をお届けします。

・株式会社ブレインスリープ
@brainsleep_official
睡眠医学に基づいた確かな知見と先進のテクノロジーを掛け合わせ、脳と睡眠を科学するソリューションカンパニーです。専門家と連携した睡眠研究、オリジナルプロダクト開発、企業やクリニックへのコンサルティングなど、睡眠に特化したあらゆるソリューションで人や社会の可能性を目覚めさせることを目指します。

・キリンビール株式会社
@kirin_brewery 
「一番搾り」「本格醸造ノンアルコール ラガーゼロ」などでおなじみの大手ビールメーカー。ととのった後の乾杯のひとときを、こだわりのおいしさで彩ります。※サウナ後の飲酒は十分な水分と休息をとってから。

・NELJAS After Sauna
@neljas_official 
ようこそ、潤いの原生林へ。オールインワン（スキンケア）ジェル「NELJAS After Sauna」。化粧品・乳液・美容液をひとつで兼ね備えた設計と、原生林の林道を彷彿とさせる香りで、サウナ愛好家に“4セット目の整い”を提案します。

・サウナド
銭湯・サウナ施設向けデジタルサイネージ「ふろビジョン」を運営する、温浴施設に特化したマーケティング企業です。

・サウナトレカ
@saunetworks 
サウナにまつわる人・モノ・施設をトレーディングカード化するプロジェクト。集めて楽しみながら推し施設を応援できます。

【協賛企業紹介①】
JSFはたくさんの協賛企業様からご協賛をいただいております。
以下にて企業様をご紹介させていただきます。

・京浜急行電鉄株式会社
@keikyu_official 
東京と羽田空港や三浦半島をつなぐ、赤い電車がシンボルの鉄道会社。川崎をはじめ沿線のまちづくりや観光振興にも力を注いでいます。平和島駅の「天然温泉 平和島」と弘明寺駅の「黒湯天然温泉 みうら湯」もご利用お待ちしております。

・大塚製薬株式会社
@pocarisweat_jp 
サウナで大量に汗をかいたカラダは、脱水状態。その水分補給には、水よりも体液の水分に近いポカリスエット イオンウォーターを。サウナでととのったカラダを、さらに「ととのえる」ことができます。ポカリスエット イオンウォーターは、水分とイオンをスムーズに補給できる健康飲料です。

・井上クリーニング株式会社
「自然と、衣類と、人々と共に。」を信念に掲げ、地元を盛り上げながら、世の中を豊かにしたいと考えております。弊社の想いにあったJapan Sauna Festivalで、今年もスポンサーを努めさせていただくことになりました。皆様が川崎で豊かにととのえることを願っております。

・saunahouse／サウナハウス
@nus_saunahouse 
川崎駅前の複合商業施設「ラ チッタデッラ」内にオープンした、シン・都市型サウナ「saunahouse（サウナハウス）」。男女それぞれに5つのサウナと温度の異なる4つの水風呂、温かいお風呂を設ける他、レストランやリラックススペースを完備。コンセプトは「ZERO DIVE」。

・黄桜株式会社
@kizakura_kappa 
2025年10月に創業100周年を迎えた京都・伏見の酒造メーカー。業界に先駆けたテレビCMや、既成概念にとらわれない商品開発で愛されてきました。「ととのいエール」は“サウナ後の最高の一杯”を目指したノンアルコールビール。カッパを大胆にあしらったパッケージも人気で、コラボサウナに加え物販ブースも出展します。

・三省製薬株式会社（IROIKU）
@iroiku_jp
IROIKUは、素肌の魅力を引き出し、健やかな肌印象を叶えるスキンケアブランド。軽やかな使い心地と心地よい香り、暮らしになじむデザインにこだわり、三省製薬が医薬品開発で培った技術と研究力を活かして生まれました。シンプルで心地よい美容習慣をあなたに。ブース出店も予定。

・株式会社サーフビバレッジ
@surfbeverage
山梨の工場で清涼飲料水の製造販売を手がける飲料メーカー。自然で良質、安全な一本を届けています。

・株式会社生活総合サービス（boco to deco／ていねい通販）
@official_teinei 
国産の明日葉とさつまいもでんぷんだけでつくった、体にも環境にもやさしい青汁「boco to deco（ボコとデコ）」。水分も栄養も不足しがちなこの季節、サウナで汗をかいた後は、野菜由来の栄養でカラダがよろこぶ一杯をいかがですか♩無料試飲ブースをご用意しておりますので、ぜひお気軽にお立ち寄りください！

・株式会社FLH（NELAX）
@hirunegao.jp 
株式会社FLHは、睡眠とリカバリーをテーマにしたブランド「NELAX」を展開。加重アイマスクをはじめ、サウナ後の“ととのい”や眠りの質を高めるプロダクトで、明日のパフォーマンスを支えます。外気浴スペースでの商品提供とブース出店（物販）を予定。

Not every surf event feels like this.

For ten days each year, Noosa slows things down a little. Longboards glide across the points, music drifts up the beach and the line between competition and good times gets pleasantly blurry.

The Noosa Festival of Surfing has built a reputation around style, flow and community  where world champs, first-timers and everyone in between somehow end up sharing the same lineup.

Less pressure. Less noise.

‘When we’re young, we learn the stories of others. When we’re adults, we create our own story. When we’re old, we tell our story.’

Please join us for a BWB Talk to celebrate the publication of Kua Tau: A Life in Stories by Tainui Stephens.
Tainui Stephens (Te Rarawa) is one of Aotearoa’s most prominent Māori storytellers. Across five decades he has been finding stories, in people, in place, and in the shifting shape of Māori life in Aotearoa. And alongside a career in filmmaking, broadcasting and cultural advocacy, he has been finding himself. Kua Tau gathers up a kete of his best writing on these subjects, drawing from his much-loved essays for the online magazine E-Tangata.
. Copies of the book will be available for sale and signing by the author.

caption: vol. 3 - moments

Punta de Lobos Pro con condiciones estelares

Punta de Lobos, la capital del surf en Chile, nos recibió con increíbles condiciones; olas que alcanzaron los 3 metros de altura y un sol resplandeciente. A esto se sumó la presentación de la categoría estelar en competencia, los Open Profesionales, tanto en damas como en varones. Así, el espectáculo estaba asegurado.

Entre quienes destacaron, podemos mencionar a Lucas Magna, de Arica, en las categorías Junior y Open. Nicolás Vargas, de Pichilemu, obtuvo 15,17 pts, mientras que Cristóbal Montecinos, de Puertecillo, logró 15,83 puntos, además de la nota más alta en lo que va del campeonato (9 pts), gracias a una combinación de roler en la parte más crítica de la ola y un sólido power surfing. Un gran desempeño para este ex seleccionado nacional que vuelve a las competencias.

Se suma a esta lista Matías Veloz, de Coquimbo, con 15,93 pts, destacando por su estilo rápido y maniobras fuertes. También Joaquín Reyes, representando a Curanipe, con un tremendo estilo de backside, fuerte y vertical (15,96 pts). Cabe mencionar la participación del mejor representante nacional en el extranjero, Roberto Araki, de Rapa Nui, quien avanzó sin problemas a la ronda 2.

En damas, Chiara Bagoni, de Coquimbo, demostró que tiene pasta de campeona, relegando al segundo puesto a la mejor representante chilena y seleccionada nacional Open, Estela López. Ambas atletas avanzaron a la ronda 2. De igual manera, destacaron Paloma Santos, de Puertecillo; y Natalia Escobar, de Pichilemu, ambas favoritas de la categoría.

En varones Sub 12, precisamente en la final ... Teodoro Romero lidero hasta prácticamente el termino de la manga, pero Beltrán Majluf, actual campeón nacional de la categoría, da vuelta el heat con una izquierda mediana que le permitió presentar hasta cuatro maniobras, todas muy bien ejecutadas, con control, fuerza y fluidez. antes de eso Moana Pakomio de Rapa Nui, presentaba una ola frente al sector el diamante que lo deja en el 2do puesto.

Ya para el final de la jornada, fuimos parte de las final sub 14 Varones y Damas, coronando como campeones a: Nicolás Durand de Puertecillo y Anania Peña de Rapa Nui .

caption:
MANY OF YOU ASKING
—
See you when the days get longer 🌱

【JAPAN SAUNA FESTIVALとは？】

JAPAN SAUNA FESTIVALは、川崎・多摩川のほとりで開催される、日本最大級のアウトドアサウナフェスです！⛺️

2025年に第1回を開催し、約1,300人の方にご来場いただきました！

川崎市・川崎市観光協会の後援のもと開催され、サウナ好きの方はもちろん、サウナ初心者の方、ご夫婦やカップル、地域の方など、幅広い方に楽しんでいただけるイベントになっております！

昨年は、

・本格的かつ様々なら種類のテントサウナ
・企業とのコラボサウナ
・チラー付きの水風呂
・100人収容の特大サウナテント
・アウフグース・熱波イベント
・サウナ飯・フード
など、アウトドアサウナを存分に楽しめるフェスとして開催しました。

そして2026年は、昨年よりさらに規模を拡大してパワーアップして開催します！

ぜひご来場お待ちしております！

BAIRROS 2026 | Quinta do Lavrado, Geração com Futuro

Com @nunocintraomusico, o workshop Constrói o Teu Som juntou participantes da @geracaocomfuturo para transformar materiais reciclados e objetos do quotidiano em instrumentos musicais.

Guitarrista, compositor e artista multidisciplinar, Nuno Cintrão trabalha há vários anos entre música, construção de objetos sonoros, teatro e projetos participativos. Aqui, trouxe essa experiência para um processo feito de construção, experimentação e improvisação, onde cada objeto ganhou novas possibilidades e o grupo foi descobrindo formas de criar música em conjunto.

A @geracaocomfuturo desenvolve trabalho de proximidade com a comunidade da Quinta do Lavrado, criando atividades e projetos que cruzam participação, educação, cultura e apoio local. Mais do que construir instrumentos, o workshop abriu espaço para ouvir, testar, inventar e fazer som com aquilo que já estava à mão.

O resultado deste processo fez parte da programação do Festival Iminente 2026.

Alarga os horizontes do teu bairro e do teu mundo.

Uma obra para partilhar!

Para o Espaço Arte Partilhada, a @fundacaomillennium – Mecenas do Festival Iminente 2026 – abriu a Coleção Millennium bcp à artista @kr.us.

A artista entrou, explorou e interpretou o acervo, desenvolvendo uma instalação criada especialmente para o festival. Por entre corredores de tecidos suspensos, transparências, bordados, pintura e escultura, os visitantes puderam encontrar e levar algumas flores têxteis feitas à mão por @kr.us. Quem partilhou o seu olhar sobre a obra, levou consigo um pedaço dela.

 Obrigado à Fundação Millennium bcp por celebrar estes 10 anos connosco. O seu apoio foi fundamental para que 20.000 visitantes vivenciassem 4 dias de Arte e concertos inesquecíveis e deste modo tornar possível continuar a criar espaço para a arte!

📷: @luuanna_ph | © Chris Costa | © Rafael Courelas
-
An artwork to share!

For the Shared Art Space, @fundacaomillennium – Patron of Festival Iminente 2026 – opened the Millennium bcp Collection to the artist @kr.us.

The artist entered, explored, and interpreted the collection, developing an installation created especially for the festival. Among corridors of suspended fabrics, transparencies, embroidery, painting, and sculpture, visitors were able to find and take home handmade textile flowers by @kr.us. Those who shared their perspective on the artwork took a piece of it with them.

Thank you to the Millennium bcp Foundation for celebrating these 10 years with us. Your support was essential for 20.000 visitors to experience 4 days of unforgettable Art and concerts, making it possible to keep creating space for art!

A Deusa do Hipocampo @lenadaguaouicestmoi no @festivaliminente 🌸
Concerto disponível na app e site da RTP Palco.

The Māoriland Indigenous Co-Lab supports filmmakers to significantly advance their feature film project over three pou. 

Pou Tuatahi - the writers lab is an 8 week residency during which writers work with mentors and tuakana to develop their next draft. It’s intense mahi which closes with table reads. 

In the days leading up to Matariki we gathered at the Māoriland Hub to hear what they’d created - six truly original stories that run the gamut from sisterly comedy to Indigenous superhero epic. 

We’re so proud of the writers - 
Matasila Freshwater with Roundabout 
Aviaq Johnston with Inuks on Vacation
Ella Gilbert with The Desert Road 
Allan George with Ancestral Fusion 
Natasha Wanganeen with Battle of the Ancestors 
Leigh Minarapa with The Keepers of the Night 

And big love and appreciation to all the actors and supporters who came out this week to be part of it.

Novidades em breve.

Durante quatro dias, a antiga Escola Afonso Domingues não foi apenas o lugar onde aconteceu o Iminente. Foi também matéria-prima.

Paredes, fachadas, janelas, estruturas e outros recantos deram origem a intervenções pensadas para este lugar; que partiram do espaço que encontraram, dialogaram com a sua arquitetura e história e passaram a fazer parte dele.

@camixvx, @3d_crew_, @43error + @pedritastudio + @furo_architecturestudio, @halfstudiosigns, @ml7_metro.lisboa, @obey_sktr, @pregos_shp, @ricardopassaporte,  @russo1003pv e @sepher.42 (com rvca_portugal).

Obras que desafiaram o olhar e mostraram que há sempre outras formas de habitar um lugar.

–

For four days, the former Escola Afonso Domingues wasn’t just the place where Iminente happened. It also became raw material.

Walls, façades, windows, structures and other corners of the School gave rise to interventions conceived specifically for this place; works that responded to the spaces they encountered, engaged with their architecture and history, and became part of them.

Contributions that challenged the way we see and showed us that there are always other ways to inhabit a place.

Araucaria Carreño, la primera campeona y la llegada del swell norte | Punta de Lobos Pro

Comenzamos con el primer día del @puntadelobospro , con condiciones bastante extrañas. El swell norte no llegaba en las primeras horas del día, lo que provocó un cambio en el itinerario, ingresando la categoría Sub 16, tanto en varones como en damas. Los atletas se las arreglaron para presentar maniobras en la zona de la cola del sector El Mirador, actuando hasta ese minuto como un beach break: ola corta, rápida y cerrona. Luego de unas horas, las olas llegaron y así también mejores maniobras, líneas más fluidas, con rollers y laybacks ya presentes.

En este intercambio, quienes sobresalieron en la Sub 16 de la primera ronda fueron: Inti Navarro con 12 pts combinados, seguido de Romano Menichetti (10,33 pts) y Nicolás Durand (10,16 pts). Ya en la ronda 2, vuelve a liderar Inti junto a Nicolás, ambos avanzando en el heat 1; los destapados de la serie fueron Pascual Marsio con 12,60 pts y el local Clemente Rodríguez con 13,33 pts. Mañana esta categoría continúa con sus respectivas semifinales.

Las jóvenes talentos no tuvieron mucha suerte en su presentación a primeras horas del día; de todas maneras, lograron concretar maniobras en las ya mencionadas olas rápidas y de rompientes fuertes. En semis se presentarán:

1: Emma Newman, Amanda Lagos y Annania Peña.
2: Amelia Hernández, Alonsa Estobar y Emma Durand.

Ya con olas de mayor tamaño fue el turno de la final Sub 12 damas, con Araucaria Carreño dejando el título en casa. La pichilemina logró correr buenas olas, apurando en los lugares correctos y buenas líneas; de esa manera relegó al segundo y tercer lugar (respectivamente) a Luciana Ríos y Mathilda Phillips.

En Sub 14 varones, los mejores puntajes fueron para Beltrán Majluf, Nicolás Durand y Moana Pakomio. En damas, la final será entre Antonella Monrroy, Annania Peña, Matilde Phillips y Araucaria Carreño.

Se cierra el día con las semifinales de Sub 12 varones, clasificando a la final: Beltrán Majluf, Teodoro Romero, Moana Pakomio y Manoa Peña.

caption:
QUEM É QUE TE CONVIDOU? 
ESTÁS SEMPRE CONVIDADO ❤️‍🔥

Quatro dias. Cinco Palcos. Uma escola inteira para descobrir.

Houve uma orquestra a sério. Festa até doer as pernas. Música, breaking, performance, dança, cinema, conversas, futebol, instalações artísticas em salas de aula, convidados surpresa e tudo o que aconteceu nos corredores pelo meio do que estava programado.

Artistas, bairros, associações, crews, equipas, amigos e desconhecidos cruzaram-se aqui. Quem vinha para ver acabou a fazer parte.

Foi assim que celebrámos 10 anos de Iminente.

Uma década a juntar o que tantas vezes aparece separado. Quem está a começar com quem já anda nisto há décadas. O bairro com o palco. Portugal com o resto do mundo. E muita gente que provavelmente nunca se encontraria noutro sítio.

A festa dos 10 anos era nossa. Mas quem fez a festa foram vocês.❤️‍🔥

Obrigado a todos os artistas, comunidades, associações, parceiros, patrocinadores, equipas e a cada pessoa que atravessou estes portões e fez parte disto.

Foram 10 anos para chegar aqui. Agora queremos saber até onde podemos ir.
–

Jessica Soekidi (@jessicasoekidi ) menelusuri pertumbuhan dan reproduksi identitas yang terus berlangsung sebagai proses dinamis dan relasional, dengan umbi-umbian sebagai inti eksplorasinya. Melalui material dan bentuk, konfigurasi yang saling terkait ini diwujudkan dalam instalasinya: umbi-umbian yang digantung, piramida terbalik yang reflektif, dan struktur totemik.

Kemarin, Jessica membuka struktur totemik tersebut untuk memanen dini umbi kentang di dalamnya. Panen ini menginterupsi siklus tumbuh alami, menyerahkan proses ‘kemenjadian’ ke tangan publik untuk mempertanyakan kembali arti keberadaan, sejarah, dan kesinambungan generasi.🥔🌱

—
Jessica Soekidi examines the growth and the ongoing reproduction of identity as a dynamic, relational process, with tubers at the core of her exploration. Through material and form, this interconnected configuration is embodied in her installation: suspended tubers, a reflective inverted pyramid, and a totemic structure.

Yesterday, Jessica opened her totemic structure to prematurely harvest the potato sprouts inside. This act interrupts the natural growth cycle, placing the process of ‘becoming’ in the hands of the public to reconsider the meaning of existence, history, and generational continuity.🍠

🪩 Jessica Soekidi, The Disco of Roots, 2026.

Zico Albaiquni (@zicoalbaiquni ) menghadirkan instalasi yang berfungsi sebagai ruang untuk memproduksi, mengganggu, dan merenegosiasi narasi. Alih-alih menampilkan karya yang selesai, Zico menyajikan lukisan dalam bentuk fragmen, seperti gambar yang beredar melalui proyeksi, cetakan, dan transparansi yang bertaut dengan sejarah, arsip kolonial, kenangan keluarga, hingga keseharian.

Instalasi ini terdiri dari empat komponen utama, yaitu proyeksi lukisan, arsip terbuka, perpustakaan kolektif, dan penulisan partisipatif. Masing-masing bagian mengajak pengunjung untuk membaca, merespons, dan meninggalkan jejak. Interaksi ini mendorong pemikiran kolektif dan perlawanan terhadap narasi sejarah yang tetap, sehingga memungkinkannya untuk dilapisi, diperdebatkan, dan dikonfigurasi ulang secara tak berujung.📗✏️

—
Zico Albaiquni creates an installation that serves as a space to produce, disturb, and renegotiate stories. Rather than presenting finished artworks, Zico offers paintings as fragments of images that circulate through projections, prints, and transparencies, intertwined with narratives involving history, colonial archives, family memories, and daily life.

This installation features four components: painting projections, open archives, a collective library, and participatory writing. Each aspect invites visitors to read, respond, and leave traces. These interactions promote collective thinking and resistance against fixed histories, allowing narratives to be layered, disputed, and endlessly reconfigured.📖🖼️ 

📚 Zico Albaiquni, Rethinking Narratives: A Reading and Writing Room, 2026.

Māoriland is proud to release our Matariki range online for 2026 —

Manu aute were flown as part of the Matariki festivities, and today that tradition is also being revitalised.
It may have been a way for those here on Papatuānuku to reach up into the domain of Ranginui to send messages to those who had passed. “Kua whakarangatia koe – Return, take your place amongst the stars along with your ancestors that adorn the sky”

Our Manu Aute collection, designed for Matariki 2026, is a collaboration between carver Fayne Robinson, his son Tahu and our directors Libby Hakaraia and Madeleine Hakaraia de Young.

We honour all those who have passed and continue to inspire us.

Matariki is a time for celebrating with feasts of kai. And so we included the well-known whakatauki; Ngā kai a Matariki nāna i ao ake ki runga. At all feasts, there are stories retold and stories created.

Māoriland celebrates the storytellers.

The 35th @noosa_festival_of_surfing was one to remember! Brandid Media was the presenting partner of the @WSL Noosa Longboard Division, as well as the entire event management and marketing engine behind the delivery of Australia’s largest surfing festival. 

The festival attracts thousands of spectators from all over the world, a record number of competitors with over 40% coming from overseas to compete, bringing millions of dollars into the local economy and delivering over 50 events. The events within the festival range from world first piano bars on the beach, insane beach parties, featuring incredible DJs, to surfing dogs, health and wellness workshops and of course a very large surfing schedule spanning over 10 days! 

Last year we hit a million views over 30 days (on Instagram only) which was a first for the festival, and our goal was to hit 1 million views over the 10 days... we tripled our goal and are still counting! 🎉

We created a strategic and detailed social media schedule, featuring daily updates, division wrap ups, post heat interviews and not to mention one of our favourite segments called @the.scoop.tv! Directed, captured and edited daily by our team, The Scoop gets all the behind the scenes action delivered straight to socials!

This year, our Live Stream had a jueje up. We created a TV style broadcast with @pangaproductions featuring advertisements for our sponsors and partners, which was also streamed in the @brixtonanz Entertainment Stage all festival long. 

We are so excited to see what we can create next year 🚀

“Everyone has a favourite. Young, old, people who sleep on the street, people who own the buildings ~ everyone has a part of it.”

In this live panel discussion from the @ncca_darwin as part of the @darwinstreetartfestival 10-year celebration, I sit down with the founder David Collins @uncooldaybed and a lineup of artists @george_rose @calebdude.art and Ris Pikala. @tom_gerrard_ hears different perspectives from established muralists to first-timers.

This conversation will inspire you.

We hear from David about the bold moment he pitched a local-run festival to the government, George about being part of four Darwin festivals, Caleb about growing up with the festival since high school and Ris about painting her first public mural.

The real story here: art isn’t just about the finished piece. It’s about the dreams it gives people. It’s about inspiration. It’s about a whole city saying “yes, this matters.”

Darwin proved it!

Created for the @charlesdarwinuniversity Casuarina Campus bus stop on Orange 1, as part of the new CDU art trail - this mural responds directly to its environment through the use of vibrant orange tones and complementary colours. 

“I wanted the work to bring a sense of energy, warmth and joy to a space that many people move through every day.

My creative process often begins with colour. From there, I explore pattern, rhythm and the relationships that emerge between shapes, lines and spaces. I’m interested in how colours interact with one another, how patterns create movement, and how the spaces between elements become just as important as the elements themselves.

Rather than telling a single story, this mural invites viewers to find their own meanings and connections. The forms can be interpreted in many ways, allowing each person to bring their own experiences, memories and imagination to the work. For me, the mural is a celebration of colour, pattern, place and the different ways we see and make meaning in the world.”

📍 CDU Casuarina Bus Stop

Meet @shopcookedconcepts, our Indigenous Program recipient for the Melbourne Design Market SS26 🎉⁠

This Aboriginal-owned Melbourne label turns local quirks into tea towels, puzzles, mugs, tote bags, apparel and more. Every design is created in Melbourne, with no stock artwork or wholesale designs in sight.⁠
⁠
Their creative process? Blue cheese before bed, then waiting for the “cultural subconscious to reveal itself” 🧀 And when we asked how they’ve grown, they told us they’re “the SCOBY of the gift world.” We’re not sure what that means either, but we love it.⁠
⁠
Behind the jokes, 25% of their profits go to the Rhodanthe Lipsett Indigenous Midwifery Charitable Fund, supporting Aboriginal people to study midwifery.⁠

Meet @fluturi.studio, our Regional Program recipient for SS26 ⁠

Every Fluturi garment starts life in a 1910 farmhouse in Tasmania’s Huon Valley, where it’s cut by hand and stitched slowly, with vintage linens and contrast pockets adding the finishing touches.⁠
⁠
After 18 years in business, their take on our “Grow” theme is a lovely one: growth doesn’t always mean getting bigger. Sometimes it’s about becoming more confident in who you are and what you make 🌱⁠

These are children’s clothes made to be worn, loved and passed on to the next little person. Even the offcuts get a second life as patchwork, reusable bags and Christmas decorations ✂️⁠

Manu aute were flown as part of the Matariki festivities, and today that tradition is also being revitalised.

Our Manu Aute collection, designed for Matariki 2026, is by carver @faynerobinson , his son Tahu and our festival director @madicattt 

We honour all those who have passed and continue to inspire us.

Matariki is a time for celebrating with feasts of kai. And so we included the well-known whakatauki; Ngā kai a Matariki nāna i ao ake ki runga. At all feasts, there are stories retold and stories created.

Māoriland celebrates the storytellers.

Karya Alif Edi Irmawan (@alifediirmawan_ ) berangkat dari isu lingkungan dengan memandang alam sebagai subjek bermartabat, bukan sebagai objek yang dapat dieksploitasi. Alief bergeser dari pendekatan informatif tentang kerusakan lingkungan menuju eksplorasi yang lebih eksistensial dan reflektif.🪾

Melalui mural masif dan deretan benda, karya ini mengubah galeri menjadi ruang ziarah kontemplatif. Pengunjung diajak hadir secara utuh dan sadar, merasakan hubungan batin dengan seluruh kehidupan di sekitarnya. Pelestarian alam pun dipahami sebagai bentuk kesetiaan terhadap kehidupan, sekaligus upaya menjaga martabat kemanusiaan.

—
Alif Edi Irmawan’s work views nature as a subject possessing its own dignity and existence. Over time, Alif’s practice has evolved from an informative approach focused on environmental degradation to a more existential and reflective exploration.

Through a monumental mural and an assemblage of objects, his artworks transform the gallery into a contemplative site of pilgrimage. The visitors are invited to be fully present and attentive, experiencing an intimate connection with all forms of life surrounding them. In this context, environmental preservation is also understood as a commitment to life itself and an effort to uphold human dignity. 🌳

🗺️ Alif Edi Irmawan, Ambang Ziarah: Mengada Dalam Keutuhan, 2026.

He taonga tuku iho te rama ataata
The light that reveals our legacies 
The artwork for this years festival was created by Lucy de Young Hakaraia. It features a takapū - a gannet - soaring across the moana and is available in @toimatarau as a silk scarf, as a limited edition print and in our limited edition MFF2026 merchandise. 

💫

Takapū are remarkable manu, perfectly adapted for soaring and for diving at high speed into the sea to catch fish. Takapū can fly more than 500km in a day, riding the wind on their outstretched two-metre wings. They leave the nest early, travelling as far as Australia and spend their first years of life on the move before returning to their homelands to nest.

Lucy de Young Hakaraia (Ngāti Kapu, Ngāti Raukawa ki te Tonga is an illustrator, animator, filmmaker and multi media artist. Her work is inspired by kōwhaiwhai and combining her designs with contemporary and graphic toi art, She has produced work for Whakauae Research, Glenn Colquhoun and AUT. Her films Waka and For Where Dreams Go have screened at Māoriland Film Festival. She is in her last year of a Bachelor of Design at AUT University.

End of Season Post 📣 We need your input, please read thank you!

What a Ride!!! The 2026 Maryhill season is over and as fall sets in, changes are coming…

We want to thank everyone who supported this event over the past year.  From the volunteers without who the event could not happen, to Miles, James, Ty, Forrest, Robin, Lexi and Ryan whose management of the workers and the event made things run smoothly.  Most importantly the riders who made the effort to travel to the event, spend a long weekend, we thank you.  Please keep coming back!

We finished the season after losing 2 long time Ratz builders of the community we have today, Ali and Andi. Their support and hard work over the years has helped shape what the Ratz are today. Words are not enough to thank them for the work they have done.

The Ratz Freerides started in 2007 with one event a year, we worked our way up to 4 events and as the industry goes through its cycles, so do we. In 2027, our 20th anniversary, we will only be putting on one event.  Community feedback has told us that Labor Day is not the best weekend. 

So what weekend would you like to see Maryhill in 2027? 

It looks like anytime between the 3rd week in May to Labor Day weekend are the choices, subject to conflicts with other events and with the road rental to other groups.  Please let us know what you think.

Also, now that the campground is developing, we think it needs a name. Any suggestions? Camp Maryhill? Maryhill Meadows? Crazy Loops Ranch? Let us know!

THANKS TO EVERYONE WHO HAS BEEN TO MARY OVER THE LAST 20 YEARS! PLEASE KEEP COMING BACK!

Ka tanuku te tihi o te maunga. Ka taka te rau o te raukura. He tohu nō aituā. E rere nei ko te awa o Wairoa, ānō nei he rere roimata ka māturuturu nei mōu e Leo kua ngaro noa. Tēnā koutou Ngāti Rakaipaaka, Ngāti Kahungunu, me te taonga ō mate ka tangihia e ngā iwi maha o te ao kiriata taketake.

Leo Koziol had a large personality. He loved to laugh. He also had a vision for film storytelling and, with the creation of the Wairoa Māori Film Festival in 2005, he gave Indigenous film a marae based platform. 

As a Māori curator of film Leo traveled the world. He always did so as a faithful child of his Wairoa iwi. His people and family are mourning him at this very moment. And so too, are many film colleagues here and overseas. He was a unique man who changed the way we think about film.

Haere rā e hoa, haere ki te pō ki reira moe mārika ai. Ko koutou ki a koutou. Ko mātou kua mahue mai, ka tangitangi nei, ka auē!

Heoi. Kia ora mai tātou katoa

We’re hosting a pop-up Italian feast at the Melbourne market next month, and you’re invited!

For one Friday night only, ‘A Feast at Nonna’s Table’ will be hosted within the market - an intimate pasta party inspired by the generosity and nostalgia of an Italian family meal.

Gianluca of @viagianlu will lovingly create the feast, drawing on his deep connection to his Italian heritage and years spent exploring regional Italian food to shape Via Gianlu’s distinctive take on Italian cuisine. Inspired by the vibrant street food culture of Italy and southern Italian traditions, Via Gianlu brings a little piece of Italy to Melbourne through food that is semplice ma gustoso – simple, generous and full of flavour.

Your feast begins with generous antipasto platters of local and imported cheeses, cured meats, olives and taralli, followed by a trio of pasta dishes featuring delicious sauces from @sorry_nonna 
🍝 Rigatoni with spicy vodka sauce
🍋 Linguine with zesty limoncello sauce
🌶️ Handmade regional cavatelli with red wine & Reaper bolognese

Come hungry, bring your favourite people and let us do the rest.

This is a Friday night-only experience, with limited seats available; once the table is full, it’s full. So get in quick and save your seat at Nonna’s Table.

E Kare Collective at Māoriland Film Festival 2026.
 
Attending MFF last month was a real milestone for our rōpu. And we felt so much warmth and manaaki during our time in Ōtaki. E mihi ana ki a koutou, te iwi ahi kā; Ngāti Raukawa ki te Tonga. The energy from kaimahi, whānau, and the wider township was unmatched. 
 
It was a real privilege to be in connection with global indigenous filmmakers. To conversate, and share cinema. We were so inspired by the whakaaro and mahi indigenous filmmakers are presenting across te ao. A beautifully diverse range of stories, risks being taken, and cinematic excellence being championed.
 
A highlight during our week was viewing the feature documentary AKI by Darlene Naponse (@darlenenaponse). What a beautiful acknowledgement of te taiao, community, reo, and time. This film pushed the boundaries of cinematic convention in such a way that remained utterly authentic. We left the festival with a commitment to explore this wero in our own practice, and we thank you for sharing it with us.
 
Till next time…
 
Image by: @andy.snaps.nz

“My intention for this mural was to incorporate elements that feel familiar and meaningful to the people of Darwin. The boab tree in the foreground is inspired by the iconic tree located in front of the city campus of @charlesdarwinuniversity. The way the tree naturally divides into two main branches created an ideal composition, framing a setting sun over a coastal landscape.

The mural combines flat planes of colour in the background with textured layers throughout the tree, creating contrast and helping to separate the foreground from the wider landscape. Elements of imagination and play are also woven into the work, with the boab tree stretched and squared at the top to respond to the unique shape of the wall and integrate with the architecture of the space.”

INSISTO NÃO SER TRISTEZA
(English below)

Na antiga Escola Afonso Domingues, o campo de futebol volta a ser ocupado.

Pintámos o verso “Insisto não ser tristeza”, de Zeca Afonso. A frase fala de uma recusa da tristeza. Não de fingir que ela não existe, mas de não a aceitar como um estado permanente. Insistir em não ser tristeza é uma forma de resistência e uma escolha de continuar, mesmo perante as dificuldades. É uma ideia que sentimos particularmente próxima dos tempos que vivemos.

As palavras distribuem-se pelo campo como jogadores em movimento, ocupando diferentes posições e criando uma composição onde se cruzam jogo, movimento e linguagem. A sua presença fala também da necessidade de insistir em ocupar, criar e não deixar que um espaço fique parado.

@festivaliminente 
Lisboa, 2026.

Vídeo: @josepandolucas 

—

I INSIST ON NOT BEING SADNESS

At the former Afonso Domingues School, the football pitch is occupied once again.

We painted the line “Insisto não ser tristeza (I insist on not being sadness)”, by Zeca Afonso. The words speak of a refusal of sadness. Not of pretending it doesn’t exist, but of refusing to accept it as a permanent state. Insisting on not being sadness becomes a form of resistance and a choice to keep going, even in the face of difficulty. It is an idea that feels particularly close to us in the times we are living through.

The words spread across the pitch like players in motion, occupying different positions and creating a composition where play, movement and language come together. Their presence also speaks of the need to insist on occupying, creating and not allowing a space to remain still.

caption:
From Papunya to Parap, Doris’ Kungka Tjuta are now dancing on the walls of Vimy Lane 💃🏽

And in many ways it’s a story come full circle. 

The history of Papunya murals is one of legend. In the early 70’s a group of Pintupi men from Papunya translated the Tjupi (Honey Ant) Dreaming Story into a mural at the local school. A story, among many others, they had painted for tens of thousands of years as traditional body paint + sand painting associated with ceremony. 

This led to the translation of stories using acrylic paint onto small boards. And this was the beginning of the Western Desert art movement, that transformed understandings of Aboriginal art and culture. It is one of the most significant art movements in Australian history. 

Doris’ husband, the late George Bush Tjangala, was a key artist in this foundational Papunya Art Movement. 

As we celebrate a decade of the legendary Darwin Street Art Festival, it feels fitting that Doris’ stories now dance across the walls of the city - carrying forward a legacy that began with the first Papunya murals more than fifty years ago 💃🏽✨

Thanks for sharing this story @darwinstreetartfestival 😘

Meet @samariarosefarm and discover Australia’s only commercial-scale Damask rose farm.
Founded by Utako and Anthony, who moved with their children to Samaria Rose Farm in regional Victoria in 2022, this chemical-free farm is home to around 2,000 Damask roses.

During the fleeting rose flowering season, the roses are hand-picked, steam-distilled, and bottled on-site, turning farm-grown fragrance into skincare and home care products from first petal to final bottle.

For the market, Samaria Rose Farm is bringing their signature Damask Rose Water and deep facial hydrating mist, both loved for their hydrating, soothing, toning and pH-balancing benefits. Visitors can grab one and get the second 50% off- the perfect excuse to gift one and keep one this festive season!

Whether you’re chasing a skincare refresh or just love a good origin story, stop by and breathe in a little piece of regional Victoria. 🌹

EVENT UDPATE - PLEASE READ - We are rapidly approaching the end of summer and that means the Tour de Maryhill/RVOD Freeride is right around the corner. Camping has become a big part of the Freeride and we are working to make it better for everyone, including fresh water and showers (ok so the showers are primitive and cold but so refreshing!). Please remember, the fire danger is extremely high so there are no open flames and do not drive in any tall grass. From the piano on “N.Y. State of Mind” to the count on “Ten Crack Commandments”. From the cuts on “Mass Appeal” to “D’Evils”. DJ Premier helped shape the sound of New York and a fundamental part of hip-hop history.

Gang Starr, Nas, The Notorious B.I.G., JAY-Z, Rakim, KRS-One, Mos Def and Jeru the Damaja all passed through his hands. Drums stripped to their core, fragments of jazz and voices cut into hooks.

That history also includes @queenbahamadia, performing at Iminente on 18 September. Premier produced “Rugged Ruff”, bringing two lines of the same legacy onto this year’s programme.

In 2026 Māoriland is excited to announce the setting up of a new space in the Māoriland Sharing Ground.

The Indigenous Arts Trading Post reclaims the idea of “trade” by removing money from the centre and restoring relationships as the true value.

Traditionally, trade was never about profit. It was about connection and reciprocity — the exchange of stories, skills, knowledge and care between communities. In a world where almost everything is bought and sold, the Indigenous Arts Trading Post invites us to return to whakawhanaungatanga — building meaningful relationships.

Artists participating in the Indigenous Arts Trading Post decide how they wish to exchange their work. Trade might take the form of conversation, collaboration, storytelling, skill-sharing or another act of reciprocity.
We invite everyone to enter this space not as consumers, but as participants in exchange.

Also at the Māoriland Sharing Ground ; An Indigenous Runway will be activated — a space to be proudly Indigenous and celebrate the tikanga of Māoriland:

 Koakoa — celebration & joy
 Ohooho — being present and alert to the moment
 Kōtahitanga — collective

Participating Artists:

and many more….

INDIGENOUS VOICES CARRY GENERATIONS OF CONNECTION TO THE WHENUA 🌿
At Māoriland, this connection isn’t just spoken about — it’s lived, practiced, and shared.
From the ocean to the whenua, these films explore our kinship with the natural world, offering ways of seeing that are rooted in relationship, responsibility, and care.
As a parakore festival, we invite you to be part of that connection — not just on screen, but in how we gather, move, and care for this place together.
Bring your reusables. Reduce your waste. Move lightly.

A moment from our performance at Bali Spirit Festival 2026. This is an excerpt of Unke Andaaz-e-Karam, the beloved ghazal-qawwali immortalized by Ustad Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, sung here by Ilahi Sufi Qawwali, the world’s first traditional women’s qawwali ensemble.

The kalam sings of love’s beautiful undoing: the beloved arrives, yet remains beyond reach, until even the heart is no longer one’s own. In the Sufi way, this very ache becomes the doorway, for the longing that empties the heart is what makes room for the Divine.

Meet our Indigenous Program recipient for the Melbourne Design Market 👋⁠
⁠
Meet Natalie of @nataliejade_art⁠
⁠
Based on Phillip Island (Millowl), Natalie is a proud Palawa woman, mother of four, and the latest in a long line of artists. She often says that paint runs through her veins, and after seeing her work, we couldn't agree more.⁠
⁠
For Natalie, painting is more than creating beautiful art. It's a journey of healing, self-discovery, and connection. Each piece offers a glimpse into her story, inspired by her family's Palawa roots, her life by the coast, and her belief that we're all deeply connected.⁠
⁠
This weekend, you'll have the chance to discover Natalie's thoughtful collection of Australian-made prints and meet the artist behind them. Her work is gentle, powerful, and full of heart, inviting us all to slow down, look a little closer, and reconnect with ourselves and the world around us.⁠
⁠
Be sure to stop by, say hello to Natalie, and experience her beautiful work in person. 💛⁠

Meet our Makers for The Melbourne Design Market this July 👋⁠

Meet @wonki.au and be the first to try their new winter flavour!

Born from an idea dreamed up by three Monash University students, Wonki creates refreshingly simple vodka sodas made with rescued fruit that would otherwise go to waste. Combining sustainability, low-sugar recipes, quality local ingredients, and a cheeky personality, the brand proves that doing good and drinking well can go hand in hand.

For Melbourne, Wonki is bringing their seasonal Winter Wonki release: Apple, Ginger & Lime. Crafted from rescued fruit and packed with refreshing flavour, this limited seasonal sip transforms produce deemed too “wonky” for supermarket shelves into something worth celebrating. Visitors can also discover the award-winning brand behind the can, recognised as Endeavour Group’s Sustainability Supplier of the Year and winner of Best in Category at the Good Design Awards.

Whether you’re passionate about reducing food waste or simply love discovering delicious new drinks, stop by and raise a can with the team helping turn unwanted fruit into seriously good sips. 🍏

Short films have always been at the heart of Māoriland.

They’re where new voices emerge, bold ideas take shape, and Indigenous storytellers share stories that travel across the world.

Some of the most unforgettable films at the festival are the shortest — bold, surprising, funny, moving, and full of imagination.

Come discover your new favourite filmmaker, or see a new work from an MFF alumni you know you love

There are 93 short films at Māoriland Film Festival - and here is every single one of them.   Short films are one of our favourite parts of the festival - getting to experience stories and spaces from all over. When we program our shorts, we think about the emotional journey we’ll take you on, how the films talk to each other when they’re paired together. 

We hope that when you come to these programs, you’ll leave bursting with conversation. 

And we’re pretty lucky to share that experience with the filmmakers in the room! 

If you’ve never been to Māoriland - start here.

Meet our Makers for The Melbourne Design Market this July 👋⁠

Meet Mel of @__may.lis__ and her exclusive market finds!

A ceramics studio celebrating the fun of imperfection, MAY.LIS creates playful, handcrafted pieces using coloured clay and the traditional Nerikomi technique. From sculptural objects to Mel’s signature ceramic bums (made from real human casts!), every piece is built slowly by hand, embracing quirks, character, and the beauty of individuality.

For Melbourne, Mel is bringing colourful nerikomi creations and playful sculptural pieces, each entirely unique and never repeated. She’ll also be releasing a limited number of exclusive commission spots for custom body-cast sculptures, complete with special lustre finishes available only through The Finders Keepers.

This July marks not only Mel’s first time at The Finders Keepers, but her very first market experience altogether. If you see her, stop by, say hello, and help us give her the warm TFK welcome our community is known for. 🫶

🌝 Low Sensory Hour 🌝⁠
⁠
We're opening early on Sunday July 12, from 9am to 10am, for Low Sensory Hour.⁠
⁠
During this time, we'll dim the lights, keep the music low or off, and keep the crowd to a minimum. We want to create a calmer and more comfortable environment for anyone who might benefit from reduced sensory stimulation.⁠
⁠
Your ticket includes general admission, so you're welcome to stay and enjoy the market after the hour ends.⁠
⁠
We've also created areas for people to pause and reset.⁠
⁠
There are various seating options and free water refill stations available throughout the venue.⁠
⁠
The Finders Keepers is for everyone, and we can't wait to welcome you in a way that feels good for you.⁠
⁠
Reserve your Low Sensory Hour ticket online for just $7 (+booking fee). Please don't wait too long - since we're accommodating fewer people at the market during this time, tickets might sell out quicker than usual. Lock in your spot now so you won't be disappointed!⁠
⁠
💫Access 💫⁠
The Royal Exhibition Building is wheelchair accessible, indoors, and the market is all on one level.⁠
⁠
Designated disabled parking is available on level P2, next to the lifts, within the Melbourne Museum car park. Wheelchairs are available for use within the venue.⁠
⁠
Assistance animals with identification are always welcome in our market venues.⁠

Meet our Makers for The Melbourne Design Market this July 👋⁠

Say hello to Jessica of @jessicajane.illustration and find her market debut goodies, only at Finders!

For nearly a decade, Jessica has been creating intricate black-and-white illustrations inspired by animals, nature, travel, stories, and the nostalgic charm of vintage books. Using traditional ink techniques like cross-hatching, stippling, and fine shading, her whimsical works invite viewers to slow down and look closer, revealing tiny details and hidden surprises with every glance.

For this Melbourne market, Jessica will be unveiling a brand-new illustration collection, making its debut at The Finders Keepers. Alongside original artwork, she’ll be bringing a range of handmade products inspired by the new piece, including greeting cards, fine art prints, stickers, bookmarks, pins, and more. Visitors will also have the chance to browse a special selection of framed original ink drawings, each showcasing the remarkable detail and craftsmanship that has become her signature.

If you’re someone who loves intricate details, whimsical storytelling, and art that reveals something new every time you look, be sure to stop by and meet Jessica this July. ✨

BAIRROS 2026 | Bairro da Curraleira / Quinta do Lavrado, Geração com Futuro

Na Quinta do Lavrado, a @galderiatakeaway não veio só ensinar gravura e serigrafia. Veio trabalhar com as imagens, as memórias e as histórias de quem conhece este território por dentro.

A Galdéria Takeaway é um projeto de criação e impressão artística que leva técnicas como a gravura e a serigrafia para fora do ateliê, promovendo processos colaborativos em diferentes contextos e comunidades. 🎨 🖼️

A partir de fotografias e arquivos ligados à antiga Curraleira, o workshop transformou memórias do bairro em matrizes, impressões e novas imagens, sob o mote “O Bairro da Curraleira Sou Eu”.

A @geracaocomfuturo trabalha diariamente com a comunidade através de iniciativas educativas, culturais, desportivas e de apoio de proximidade, reforçando relações e criando novas oportunidades dentro do bairro.

Entre linóleo, tinta, papel e muitas mãos à obra, começou a construir-se um arquivo visual feito com a comunidade, e não apenas sobre ela. O processo deixa também ferramentas e conhecimentos na Geração com Futuro, para que esta oficina possa continuar para lá destes encontros.

O resultado será apresentado no Festival Iminente, de 17 a 20 de setembro.

Alarga os horizontes do teu bairro e do teu mundo.

Meet our Regional Program recipient for The Melbourne Design Market this July 👋⁠
⁠
Meet Natasha of @wildwoodpages⁠
⁠
Based in Atherton in Far North Queensland, Wildwood Pages creates beautifully crafted timber notebooks designed to be treasured, gifted, and filled with ideas, sketches, plans, stories, and dreams. Every notebook begins in Tash's regional workshop, where sheets of plywood are carefully designed, stained, sanded, laser-cut, assembled, and finished by hand, transforming simple materials into keepsakes built to last.⁠
⁠
This July marks Tash's first market with The Finders Keepers, thanks to our Regional Program, which supports talented makers from across outer regional and remote Australia. In Melbourne, she'll launch four brand-new notebook designs, available to discover at the market before they're released anywhere else.⁠
⁠
Living and working regionally has shaped Tash's approach to her craft. Inspired by the slower pace of country life, she creates pieces that encourage people to pause, reflect, and reconnect with their creativity in a world that often feels rushed and distracted.⁠
⁠
Whether you're searching for a thoughtful gift, a place to capture your next big idea, or simply a reason to put pen to paper again, be sure to stop by and meet Tash this July.⁠

BAIRROS 2026 | Beato – Associação de Moradores Viver Melhor no Beato

Na VMBA, @omiri_official não veio só trabalhar música. Veio escutar o bairro, as suas histórias, os seus sons e os seus sonhos.

O workshop aconteceu com o grupo sénior da Associação de Moradores Viver Melhor no Beato, uma associação ativa na Picheleira desde 2011, que promove o desenvolvimento social, cultural e comunitário através de projetos participativos e de proximidade.

Omiri, projeto de Vasco Ribeiro Casais, reinventa a música de raiz portuguesa a partir de recolhas sonoras e visuais, cruzando tradição, memória e experimentação. No Beato, essa escuta passou pelas rotinas, pelas vozes e pelos imaginários de quem vive ali todos os dias.

Entre partilhas, sons captados, objetos transformados em instrumentos e ritmos criados em conjunto, começou a nascer uma paisagem sonora feita com a comunidade, e não apenas sobre ela.

O resultado será apresentado no Festival Iminente, de 17 a 20 de setembro.

Alarga os horizontes do teu bairro e do teu mundo.

Na VMBA, @arashida não veio só pintar um campo. Veio ajudar a transformar um espaço conquistado pelo bairro num lugar com mais cor, pertença e identidade.

O workshop aconteceu com jovens da @associacao_moradores_vmba no Beato, uma associação ativa na Picheleira desde 2011, que promove o desenvolvimento social, cultural e comunitário através de projetos participativos e de proximidade.

Arashida, artista visual e ilustradora brasileira a viver em Portugal, trabalha a partir da memória, da cultura popular, dos corpos e dos rituais em movimento. No Beato, trouxe essa linguagem para um processo coletivo de imaginação e intervenção no espaço público.

Entre conversas, desenhos, ideias partilhadas e muitas mãos a colorir, o campo de futebol começou a ganhar uma nova vida — pensada com quem o usa, o atravessa e o reconhece como seu.

Porque ocupar a cidade também é isto: deixar marca nos lugares que fazem parte da nossa história todos os dias.

Alarga os horizontes do teu bairro e do teu mundo.

caption:
Na sequência do que foi publicado na comunicação social, recebemos algumas perguntas sobre as pessoas que vivem na antiga Escola Afonso Domingues, onde terá lugar a 10.ª edição do Iminente.

Mantivemos este processo fora das redes sociais por respeito e pela privacidade de quem ali vive. Esperámos até que se encontrasse uma solução real para estas pessoas, e acreditamos que esse dia chegou. 

Desde o início, temos trabalhado com a Câmara Municipal de Lisboa, parceiros sociais e serviços de apoio na procura de alternativas de habitação individuais e dignas, cuja aceitação cabe sempre às próprias pessoas. 

Quem decidir não aceitar pode permanecer no espaço. O festival está desenhado para acontecer sem ocupar as áreas onde estas pessoas vivem. Nunca expulsámos, nem vamos expulsar, ninguém. Não celebraríamos 10 anos de Iminente à custa da falta de habitação de quem quer que seja.

A indignação é legítima. O que se faz com ela é que importa.

caption:
Ilahi Sufi Qawwali performing “Unke Andaaz-e-Karam” live at Bali Spirit Festival 2026.

This Kalam by Pir Syed Naseeruddin Naseer of Golra Sharif speaks of the beloved whose grace both undoes and remakes the heart. 
It moves through the ache of unfulfilled longing, the surrender that love demands, and the quiet truth that ishq is no game but a path that unravels the self entirely. 
What begins as a glance ends in annihilation, the heart erased so that only the beloved remains. 

The Sufi master composed this alongside our teachers Ustad Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan and Ustad Dildar Hussain, a lineage we carry with deep reverence.

Ilahi Sufi Qawwali is a group of women from different parts of the world learning this sacred art at the Sama School of Music in Bali, an initiative to support women who wish to study Qawwali, a tradition that has been carried almost entirely by men for centuries. 
We are still on the path. This music asks for a lifetime, and we walk it with patience and devotion. The group is taught by Tahir Qawwal, who has devoted his life to learning this music with his Ustads in Pakistan and leads the internationally acclaimed ensemble Fanna-Fi-Allah Sufi Qawwali.

Nemanja Bošković uses contemporary dance and improvisation to create dialogue and presence in public space.

Their work will unfold through encounters with local communities and the city itself. Stay tuned!

Rox is the person behind the curation and creative magic of our markets. She reads every single application (yes, hundreds of them 😅), carefully shapes our stallholder line-ups, and helps turn big ideas into meaningful experiences.⁠

She’s passionate about creating little “pockets of wow”, the kind of moments that make people stop, smile, explore, connect, and feel part of something special. Vivemos numa era em que termos carregados, como “lenda”, “ícone” e “épico”, se usam levianamente. Um tempo de heróis e egos inflacionados.

De vez em quando, damos de frente com um artista a quem a coroa assenta na perfeição. Com alguma sorte, presenciamos a sua mestria em primeira mão. Para celebrar 20 anos no Forte de Santiago da Barra, e o regresso às nossas raízes ANTIPOP, trazemos de volta o nosso amigo Laurent Garnier para a última dança, a última viagem, Le Grand Finale, com a lenda no comando.

*

We live in an age where heavy words like “epic”, “legendary” and “iconic” are lightly thrown. A time of ephemeral heroes and giant egos.

Rarely, we crash into someone who merits every superlative that is thrown their way, if we are lucky, we get to know them beyond the surface. To celebrate 20 years of history, and the return to our ANTIPOP roots, we bring back our friend Laurent Garnier for one last pull of the curtain, one last journey, one last dance, Le Grand Finale, with the legend himself.

_

I never dreamed of being a DJ. 

Drumming took me on a few laps around the world, deeper into foreign cultures, where the rhythm was the common language. 

But after a while I needed to lead. To really move a room from my own heartbeat, my expression, on my own terms. 
(without the risk of being replaced by a loop pedal and stomp box 😆)

DJing gave me my wings, drumming at the same time keeps me grounded. 

Somehow it all worked out and it’s currently feeding my family. Music connects us every single day.

We are very happy that our film Back to Nogliki has become part of the Māoriland Film Festival.

It is one of the largest Indigenous film festivals in the world, held in the town of Ōtaki, bringing together filmmakers and audiences from across the globe.

It is especially meaningful for us that a story filmed on Sakhalin, on Nivkh land, will exist within this space. That the voice of the small settlement of Nogliki will be heard so far away — among other Indigenous voices.

It feels almost impossible that the path of this film crosses the ocean.

Thank you, Māoriland, for your trust and for creating space for this conversation.

Мы очень рады, что фильм «Назад в Ноглики» стал частью Māoriland Film Festival. 

Это один из крупнейших фестивалей кино коренных народов в мире, который проходит в городе Ōtaki и собирает режиссёров и зрителей со всего мира. 

Для нас очень важно, что история, снятая на Сахалине, среди нивхской земли, станет частью этого пространства. Что голос небольшого посёлка Ноглики прозвучит так далеко — среди других голосов коренных народов. Кажется почти невозможным, что путь этого фильма проходит через океан. 

Спасибо Māoriland за доверие и пространство для этого разговора.

UNFOLD is a European cooperation project that connects artists, communities and public space across Portugal, Serbia and Greece. Co-funded by the European Union (@europacriativa_pt), it focuses on how artistic practices can activate cities, create dialogue and engage people who are not usually part of cultural programmes.

At its core is an exchange between countries, where each partner sends artists abroad and hosts international artists locally. In Portugal, two artists will develop work in other contexts, while Iminente welcomes artists from Serbia and Greece to work in Lisbon.

Rather than working only in traditional venues, UNFOLD takes place in everyday spaces, working closely with local communities and contexts.

In Lisbon, UNFOLD is hosted by Iminente, who leads the local programme and welcomes international artists to develop artistic interventions in the city, in connection with local realities and communities. This process will unfold over the coming months and will culminate in a public moment at Iminente Festival, in September.

The project is developed together with @balkansbeyond in Greece and @ugklarairosa in Serbia. More soon.

What is UNFOLD's fellowship programme?
The UNFOLD fellowship is a 9-month programme that brings together 12 artists from Portugal, Serbia and Greece to learn, exchange and develop work in close connection with communities.
Through masterclasses, mentoring and collaborative research, artists explore how to work in public space and engage with different local contexts. Each artist also takes part in an international exchange, developing work abroad while hosting artists in their own city.
The process culminates in artistic interventions in each country, including Lisbon, hosted by Iminente.

Stay tuned for more details!

This project is funded by Creative Europe (@europacriativa_pt)
Partners:@ugklarairosa @balkansbeyond

O que é o programa de fellowship UNFOLD?
O fellowship do UNFOLD é um programa de 9 meses que reúne 12 artistas de Portugal, Sérvia e Grécia para aprender, trocar experiências e desenvolver trabalho em ligação próxima com comunidades.
Através de masterclasses, mentoria e investigação colaborativa, os artistas exploram formas de trabalhar no espaço público e de se relacionar com diferentes contextos locais. Cada artista participa também num intercâmbio internacional, desenvolvendo trabalho noutros países e acolhendo artistas na sua própria cidade.
O processo culmina em intervenções artísticas em cada país, incluindo Lisboa, com acolhimento do Iminente.

BAIRROS 2025 | Curraleira – Geração com Futuro

Reinventar. Repensar. Reivindicar.
Este ano, o bairro da Curraleira e a @geracaocomfuturo transformaram-se em palcos de mudança – moldados por muitas mãos, histórias e imaginação partilhada.

A artista visual @vaidarpitanga orientou um workshop dinâmico de upcycling que deu vida nova a roupas descartadas, transformando-as em manifestações de criatividade e protesto. Os pincéis tornaram-se ferramentas de resistência. Os tecidos, em telas para ideias arrojadas. O resultado? Um desfile de moda reciclada onde cada peça desfilou com propósito – revelando a visão dos participantes e um posicionamento coletivo contra o desperdício.

Ao mesmo tempo, o artista e escultor @migueldesousacardinho retomou uma história iniciada em 2024: um projeto para aproximar os livros dos jovens leitores. Dando continuidade à biblioteca móvel criada no ano anterior, concebeu um conjunto de mesas e cadeiras feitas à medida para apoiar sessões de leitura e atividades de mediação na associação e nas suas imediações – objetos pensados não apenas para a funcionalidade, mas para promover encontro, cuidado e criatividade.
–
Reinvent. Rethink. Reclaim.
This year, the Curraleira neighbourhood and @geracaocomfuturo became a stage for transformation – shaped by many hands, stories, and shared imagination.

Visual artist @vaidarpitanga led a vibrant upcycling workshop that turned discarded clothes into statements of creativity and protest. Brushes became tools of resistance. Fabric, a canvas for bold ideas. The result? A recycled fashion show where each piece walked with purpose – reflecting the participants’ visions and a collective stand against waste.

Meanwhile, artist and sculptor @migueldesousacardinho revisited a 2024 project to bring books closer to young readers. Building on last year’s mobile library, he designed custom tables and chairs for reading sessions and activities – pieces made for function, togetherness, and creativity.

caption:
BAIRROS 2025 | PER7 – Associação Bairro Quinta Grande

Criar e ocupar espaço.
O que falta no bairro? É uma pergunta que desencadeia uma enxurrada de respostas. Vez após vez, surgem as mesmas: um sítio para sentar. Espaços de convívio. Um pouco de sombra.

O designer @joao__xara respondeu com um exercício criativo de design de mobiliário – mas, mais do que isso, com um workshop que convidou os participantes a refletir sobre esta ausência. Ao fazê-lo, lançou luz sobre as desigualdades que separam este território de outras zonas de Lisboa. Aqui, o design torna-se uma forma de escuta, de reconhecimento e de imaginação sobre um espaço público diferente.

Em paralelo, os músicos e produtores @fumaxabeatz e @daus.pt voltaram à Associação Bairro da Quinta Grande para trabalhar com uma comunidade de participantes que tem explorado o som e a criação ao longo dos anos. Juntos, criaram um conjunto de novos temas que serão, em breve, lançados para o mundo.

Isto é o BAIRROS: um espaço para pensar, construir e fazer ressoar novas formas de pertença.
–
What’s missing in the neighbourhood? It’s a question that opens a flood of reactions. Again and again, the answers emerge: somewhere to sit. Places to gather. A bit of shade.

Designer @joao__xara responded with a creative exercise in furniture design – but more than that, with a workshop that asked participants to reflect on this absence. In doing so, it cast light on the inequalities that separate this territory from other areas of Lisbon. Design here becomes a form of listening, of acknowledging, and of imagining a different kind of public space.

In parallel, musicians and producers @fumaxabeatz and @daus.pt returned to the Bairro da Quinta Grande Association to work with a community of participants who have been exploring sound and creation over the years. Together, they created a new set of tracks that will soon be released to the world.

This is BAIRROS: a space to think, to build, to sound out new ways of belonging.
–

Pintar, plantar, reparar.
Na @associacao_de_moradores_per11, comunidade é sinónimo de ação. Do apoio ao estudo à costura, da ginástica à reparação de bicicletas, a associação é uma rede viva de cuidado, solidariedade e autossuficiência. Há uma frase que diz tudo: estamos juntos.

O artista visual @manel.alma deu forma a esse espírito com um workshop centrado na transformação do contentor onde se guardam dezenas de bicicletas recuperadas e partilhadas pelos moradores. Entre pinceladas coletivas e criações individuais em azulejo, os participantes deram corpo a um espaço que guarda tanto a memória como o movimento.

Ao mesmo tempo, a @flordemurtaassociacao criou raízes — literalmente. Recuperando o espírito perdido na transição das barracas para os apartamentos, convidou a comunidade a co-criar um jardim que é uma horta comunitária e também um espaço de convívio. Através de workshops que uniram ecologia e cultura, cultivaram-se plantas, relações e um renovado sentido de pertença.
–
At @associacao_de_moradores_per11, community means action. From tutoring to sewing, gymnastics to bike repair, the association is a living network of care, solidarity, and self-reliance. One phrase says it all: we’re in this together.

Visual artist @manel.alma brought that spirit to life with a workshop focused on transforming the bicycle container – a vital hub for the dozens of bikes repaired and shared by residents. Through collective painting and individual tile-making, participants gave shape to a space that holds both memory and movement.

At the same time, @flordemurtaassociacao put down roots — literally. Reviving the spirit lost in the transition from shacks to apartments, it invited the community to co-create a garden that is both a community vegetable patch and a shared gathering space. Through workshops that brought together ecology and culture, they cultivated not only plants but also relationships and a renewed sense of belonging.
–

Welcome to the 2026 Zine Game Jam run by sticky institute! 
The goal of this Jam is to make at least ONE GAME ZINE! 
The world can always use more zines and especially GAME ZINES!

The theme of this Jam is “A pack of Playing Cards”

The game must somehow include the use of a single deck of cards and a Zine. This can either be including the pack of cards in the theme or using the pack of cards as the primary tool the game functions off of. 

Last year that this ran, there were many questions about what even is a zine? A zine is just a book, just information formatted into a small pamphlet either physically or a PDF for online purposes. It is an intensely nebulous thing. A rule book is Zine enough, if you can put the rules for how to play your game into this format, congrats! You’ve made a game zine!

Our music video for “Find My Way Back” has just been announced as an official selection at @maorilandfilm Festival.

This will be our third trip back to Māoriland  a festival that uplifts Indigenous voices from around the world

I’ve recently learned that my great great great grandfather, Hitiri Te Paerata, was a rangatira (leader) of Ngāti Raukawa— an iwi connected to those lands.

And now, generations later, I’m bringing a story called “Find My Way Back” home.

When we created this work, I didn’t consciously know that connection yet.
 I just knew I was writing from a place of longing… identity… healing… return.
The whakapapa knew.
This selection feels bigger than a milestone. It feels like a thread being pulled across time. A reminder that even when we wander, we are always being guided back.
To my tīpuna — thank you for walking before me. To my whānau — this is ours. To everyone who helped bring this vision to life — thank you for holding it with such care.
We are always finding our way back 🤍

#FindMyWayBack #Māoriland #NgātiRaukawa #Whakapapa #IndigenousStorytelling OfficialSelection

来年で設立30周年を迎える、世界最高峰のレコードショップ／レーベル「Rush Hour」。その創設者であり、類稀なる審美眼と確かな技術で世界中のダンスフロアを魅了し続けるDJ、Antalを迎えた「Listening Session」を10月10日 (土) に1 Hotel Tokyoで開催します。

本セッションでは、「自身の人生に影響を与えた楽曲」や「Rush Hourの歩みを象徴する名曲」などをテーマに、Antal自身が厳選したレコードを聴きながら、彼の音楽的ルーツや哲学をインタビューとともに紐解いていきます。

サウンドシステムは英国のダンスミュージックシーンにルーツを持ち、国産木材を用いた卓越した造形で知られるスピーカーブランド「Higo Beat」。そして、最高峰の音響性能を誇るハイエンド・ロータリーミキサー「Cometa M2」。この特別な環境で味わう、美しく響く極上の音楽体験を1 Hotel Tokyo でご堪能ください。50枚限定の前売券発売開始 🎫

To celebrate the upcoming 30th anniversary next year of Rush Hour, one of the world's most acclaimed record shops and labels, we are proud to host a special Listening Session featuring its founder, Antal, a DJ renowned worldwide for his exceptional curation and technical prowess.

During this session, Antal will play a selection of personal vinyl records that have  influenced his life and career, as well as defining releases from Rush Hour’s history. Through these vinyl records and an intimate interview, we will delve into his musical roots and underlying musical philosophy.

The sound system features Higo Beat - a custom speaker brand rooted in British dance music culture and hand-crafted with domestic Japanese timber - paired with the Cometa M2 - a top-tier rotary DJ mixer celebrated for its exceptional audio fidelity and sleek design. Join us for an extraordinary listening experience set within a truly refined soundscape at 1 Hotel Tokyo.

Joseph Capriati e Luke Slater encontram-se num formato que dispensa grandes apresentações. Dois percursos distintos, cruzados por décadas de pista, estúdio e evolução constante.

Neste encontro o passado está presente sem pesar, e o momento ganha outra dimensão quando partilhado. O resto resolve-se onde faz mais sentido: na pista de dança.

*

Joseph Capriati and Luke Slater come together in a format that needs no introduction. Two distinct journeys, shaped by decades on dancefloors, in studios, and through constant evolution.

Ever been curious about zines? Well maybe you should talk to this guy, Luke Sticky (Sinclair), co-founder of @sticky_institute and Festival of the Photocopier, the tectonic movement behind @smallzinevolcano, creator of the over-two-decades-old weekly zine YOU, and co-host of ZINE! with Cora Zon on Yarra Valley FM, where you might hear him describe a zine as an independent publication. A small handmade magazine. Usually made by an individual or a small group of individuals. Often stapled. Often photocopied. Made with honesty, and always for love and not for profit.
Then, he'll tell you a zine can break one or all of those rules and still be a zine. He might tell you about zine distros that have come and gone. Sticky's near misses. About a zine he loves. The role of zine fairs. And about how, sometimes, once you've made one zine, it becomes a thing that just has to keep happening.
Read his interview with Liz and Ronnie now on folicomics.com.

ロンドンのアンダーグラウンド・シーンを強烈な求心力で牽引する要塞クラブ「FOLD」と、日本を代表するダンスミュージックフェスティバル「Rainbow Disco Club」によるコラボレーション・イベントがWOMBで実現。ロンドンのインダストリアルな熱気と、RDCが培ってきた祝祭の要素が3つのフロアで激突・融合する。それぞれのフロアが全く異なるストーリーを描きながらも、一つのうねりとなって朝まで駆け抜ける、妥協なきキュレーションを体感してほしい。

2FではFOLDの熱気と日本のテクノ・シーンが共鳴する。ロンドンFOLDの狂騒をそのままパッケージしたかのような、ディープでエネルギッシュな空間となるだろう。FOLDのキーマンであるVoicedrone b2b James Newmarchがロンドンから直輸入のバウンシーかつインダストリアルなグルーヴを投下する。迎え撃つ日本勢は、本国のFOLDにも出演経験のあるストイックな探求でフロアを支配するHarukaと、国内外で躍進を続けトランシーかつ催眠的なセットで魅了するDJ Maria.だ。また、本公演でDJ Maria.は「Non Techno Set」と題したスペシャルなセットを披露する。

4Fでは深淵なるサイケデリックとオルタナティブの探求、音楽の深みへの没入体験がクラバーたちを待ち受ける。予測不能な異空間、ドロドロとした独自のサウンドスケープでフロアを底なしの沼へと引きずり込む悪魔の沼と、日本のオルタナティブ・ディスコ〜レフトフィールド・シーンの至宝Kenji Takimiが共演を果たす。妖しくも美しいコズミック・グルーヴと、サイケデリックな電子音が混ざり合う、中毒性の高い音楽体験がここにはある。

1Fはローカルの活気が溢れる豊潤なハウスやディスコで空間を暖かく彩るダンスフロアになるだろう。DJツアーと並行して果敢なプロデュースで世界に羽ばたいているMayurashkaと、安定感のある選曲でフロアに規律をもたらすCYKのNariがラインナップ。この2人を、RDCのレジデント Kikiorix が迎え撃つ。

国境を越え、ロンドンと日本のダンスミュージック・コミュニティが深く交じり合う特別なショーケース。この歴史的な交差点をお見逃しなく。

BEST004 - The Melting Hours - The Melting Hours EP

Out today on Beyond Space And Time: The Melting Hours, the debut EP by The Melting Hours, a live project by Wata Igarashi and Kuniyuki.

Available now on vinyl, digital, Bandcamp and all streaming platforms.

Written, Performed, Recorded and Mixed by Wata Igarashi & Kuniyuki Takahashi
Wata Igarashi - Guitars, Synthesizers and Electronics
Kuniyuki Takahashi - Synthesizers, Drum Machines, Percussions and Flute

Mastered by MaSpaventi @maspaventimastering 
Artwork by Kikiorix @kikigraphix 

It brings to mind the Rainbow Disco Club event back in 2026, where they wove their sounds amidst fresh greenery and surrounded by listeners under a clear blue sky. It felt as though the pulsating energy was spreading across the dance floor, guided by a session from The Melting Hours that seemed almost like a living creature. The organic breath one senses in this work not only evokes precisely that scene but also allows us to feel the unique, ephemeral nature inherent in this project—and, consequently, the boundless possibilities that stem from it.

BEST004 - The Melting Hours - The Melting Hours EP

The latest release from Rainbow Disco Club’s label imprint, Beyond Space And Time, is the debut compilation from The Melting Hours, a live project by Wata Igarashi and Kuniyuki. Wata Igarashi continues to make his mark on the history of techno, whilst Kuniyuki has long been revered as one of Sapporo’s greatest treasures. The two artists, who have long held mutual respect for one another, met whilst performing at the Draaimolen Festival 2025, and this encounter gave rise to The Melting Hours.

‘Blue Sun’ is imbued with a freshness reminiscent of the ambient jazz masterpieces released by prestigious labels such as ECM and Windham Hill. ‘Liquid Dunes’ sees the organic tones of the flute and percussion melt into over ten minutes of abstract sound textures, whilst the breathtaking ‘Cloud Touch’ awakens amidst a swirling vortex of pulsating downbeats and arpeggios. It is said that ‘Blue Sun’ was created by reconstructing studio rehearsal recordings, whilst ‘Liquid Dunes’ and ‘Cloud Touch’ were crafted from live recordings at Draaimolen 2025. The essence of these works—and indeed of the project The Melting Hours itself—lies at the heart of their improvisational nature.

It brings to mind the Rainbow Disco Club event back in 2026, where they wove their sounds amidst fresh greenery and surrounded by listeners under a clear blue sky. It felt as though the pulsating energy was spreading across the dance floor, guided by a session from The Melting Hours that seemed almost like a living creature. The organic breath one senses in this work not only evokes precisely that scene but also allows us to feel the unique, ephemeral nature inherent in this project—and, consequently, the boundless possibilities that stem from it.

Release Date: 1st October 2026

How do you grow a festival without losing its “feeling”?

For 17 years, Rainbow Disco Club has built its own rhythm from a hillside in Shizuoka, where daytime dancing, thoughtful programming and a close relationship with nature shape the festival experience.

We spoke with founder Masahiro Tsuchiya and director Yuki Yokoyama as they reflect on RDC’s “Beyond Space And Time” philosophy, expanding beyond Japan, building long-term community partnerships and keeping the festival true to itself.

As Tsuchiya puts it, the feeling is “kind of like going on a picnic with friends.”

17 years of lessons to be shared; read the full interview via linkinbio.

昨日6月9日、我々が誇るRDCレジデントSisiの49日の法要が行われました。彼を愛した多くの人たちが集まり、今一度彼の残した軌跡と愛を感じました。

彼が人生を賭けて情熱を注いだ音楽は国境、世代を超えて、多くの人々の人生に刻まれていることだと思います。RDCチームも同様に彼の音楽、人柄に胸を打たれ、人生に多大な影響を与えられました。

ここから我々は再度、歩み始めるわけですが、その前に彼が残した素敵なセットをもう1つ公開いたします。

彼が生前多くの時間を共に過ごし、彼の遺伝子を大きく受け継いでいるKlymaxのレジデントであるGeroとの昨年12月に開催されたWonderfruitでのB2Bセットです。2人が紡いだ音楽はフェスティバルの最終日の夜明けをこれ以上になく彩りました。
間違いなくただその日の夜明けであっただけではなく、さまざまな人の心に太陽を照らした瞬間でした。

Sisi、ありがとう！またいつか！

Yesterday, June 9, we held a memorial service marking the 49th day since the passing of our beloved resident DJ, Sisi. Many people who loved him gathered to once again reflect on the legacy he left behind and the love he shared.

I believe the music to which he dedicated his life and poured his passion has transcended borders and generations, leaving an indelible mark on the lives of so many people.
We, the RDC team, were equally moved by his music and his character, and he had a profound impact on our lives.

As we set out on this new journey, we would like to share one more of the wonderful sets he left behind.

It’s a B2B set from Wonderfruit last December with Gero, a Klymax resident who spent a great deal of time with him during his lifetime and carries on much of his music identity. The music they created together perfectly illuminated the dawn of the festival’s final day.
It was undoubtedly not just the dawn of that day, but a moment that shone a ray of sunshine into the hearts of so many people.

Sisi, forever!!

RDCレジデントDJ Sisi 逝去のお知らせ

Sisiが2026年4月22日、脳内出血により46歳の若さで永眠いたしました。先ほど葬儀を終え、最期の別れをしてきました。葬儀を終えるまでSNSでのご報告を控えておりましたことを、何卒ご理解ください。

2013年にレジデントとなって以来、彼は長年にわたりRDCの音楽的支柱であり続けてくれました。卓越したセンスを持つDJであり、情熱的なレコードディガーでもあったSisiは、その唯一無二の選曲とプレイで、私たちに計り知れない影響を与えてくれました。

2013年の中国でのプレイを皮切りに、世界各地で開催されたRDCの海外公演に出演し、シーンに確かな足跡を刻みました。特にアジアにおいては、多くのダンスフロアに強烈な印象を残し、今なお語り継がれるような瞬間を幾度も生み出してきました。

このたび、SisiがRDC関連のパーティーとして最後にソロ出演した「RDC × Love International」のセットを公開いたします。彼の音楽がどれだけ自由で、深く、人々の心を動かしてきたのかを、ぜひ感じてください。

Sisiが紡いできた音楽は、これからも私たちの中で鳴り続けます。ダンスフロアで交わした無数の瞬間、音に溶けていった記憶、そのすべてが今も確かにここにあります。

どうか安らかに。
我々はこれからも、あなたの遺した音楽と共に歩み続けます。

Announcement of the Passing of RDC Resident DJ Sisi

Sisi passed away on 22 April 2026 at the young age of 46 following a cerebral haemorrhage. We have just attended his funeral and said our final goodbyes. We ask for your understanding regarding our decision to refrain from making any announcements on social media until the funeral had taken place.

Since becoming a resident in 2013, he remained a musical pillar of RDC for many years. A DJ of exceptional taste and a passionate record digger, Sisi had an immeasurable influence on us through his unique track selection and performance style.

Starting with his set in China in 2013, he performed at RDC’s overseas shows held around the world, leaving an indelible mark on the scene. In Asia in particular, he left a powerful impression on countless dancefloors, creating moments that are still talked about to this day.

We are now releasing the set from ‘RDC × Love International’, which was Sisi’s final solo performance at an RDC-related party. We invite you to experience just how free and profound his music was, and how deeply it moved people’s hearts.

The music Sisi created will continue to resonate within us. The countless moments shared on the dance floor, the memories that melted into the sound—all of it remains here with us today.

Rest in peace.
We will continue to walk alongside the music you left behind.
