Jiggy B2B The Advent, dois dos expoentes máximos da história lusa na música eletrónica. Kaos Records, Alcântara-Mar, Tresor, Klockworks… entre os dois, intervieram em quase tudo o que mexeu e continua a mexer no techno mundial, tendo produzido, mixado e (claro!) inspirado centenas de faixas, singles e álbuns ao longo de três décadas de carreira.

Este ano, acrescentam à lista uma aparição conjunta nos 20 anos do NEOPOP Festival, que promete não deixar ninguém indiferente.

*

Jiggy B2B The Advent, it wouldn’t be an exaggeration to call them two of Portugal’s most influential exports when it comes to electronic music. Between imprints like the legendary Kaos records, Tresor and Klockworks, both artists touched upon practically everything that shook the airwaves in the scene, being highly coveted and constantly credited as producers, mixers, and (of course!) inspiration for hundreds of tracks, singles and albums over three decades in the business.

This year they add a back-to-back performance at NEOPOP Festival’s 20th anniversary to that long record of leaving no one indifferent.

Confirmadas las fechas de La Serena y Pichilemu para el Circuito Nacional

El surf nacional entra en su etapa más vibrante de la temporada. Bajo el marco de @surfestival , se han oficializado la 2da y 3ra fecha del Circuito Chileno de Surf (Fechsurf), eventos que reunirán a las promesas y figuras consolidadas del deporte en dos de las locaciones más icónicas del país: La Serena y Pichilemu.

La Serena Pro 2026: El retorno a un escenario histórico .- 

La acción comienza los días 27 y 28 de enero en la Av. Del Mar, específicamente en la Escuela de Surf Poisson @escuelasurfpoisson . La Serena Pro 2026 by Surfestival @surfestivalaserena , regresa a uno de los puntos más emblemáticos del circuito veraniego. Este evento, de categoría 2 Estrellas (500 puntos para el ranking), repartirá $3.000.000 en premios y contará con las categorías federadas Sub 16 y Junior (Damas y Varones), además de una espectacular Expression Session en categoría Open.

Punta de Lobos Pro 2026: Competencia en la capital del surf.- 

Siguiendo con el calendario, del 9 al 11 de febrero, la competencia se traslada a la Región de O’Higgins para el Punta de Lobos Pro 2026 @puntadelobospro . En el mítico sector de El Mirador de Punta de Lobos; los mejores surfistas del país se enfrentarán en la 3ra fecha del Circuito Nacional, evento que servirá de antesala al Surfestival Pichilemu @surfestival , a realizarse el 14 de febrero.

Esta 3ra fecha del circuito nacional incluirá un rango más amplio de categorías formativas (Sub 12, Sub 14, Sub 16 y Junior), junto a la categoría principal que es Open; todas
federadas en Damas y Varones, para la cual se mantendrá la bolsa de $3.000.000 en premios a repartir y las 2 estrellas. 

La cobertura oficial de los eventos deportivos estará a cargo de Latinwave @latinwave.cl y se podrá ver más detalles en las cuentas de instagram de ambos eventos @laserenapro y

Radi Arwinda (1983-2025) (@radiarwinda ) merefleksikan proses eksplorasi diri di tengah pertemuan dua budaya. Budaya Sunda dari Cirebon mengakar kuat dalam lingkungan keluarga. Seiring waktu, pengaruh budaya pop kontemporer yang mulai masuk menimbulkan konflik identitas dalam dirinya.🏠🌎

Menandai babak baru dalam proses penemuan diri, Radi memadukan simbol budaya populer dan ornamen tradisional dalam karyanya. Praktik artistiknya melampaui apresiasi budaya yang hanya bersifat permukaan, melainkan mencerminkan adaptasi budaya lokal terhadap dunia yang serba cepat dan tidak menentu.

Karya-karya Radi Arwinda hadir di ARTJOG sebagai bentuk penghormatan terhadap dirinya sekaligus melanjutkan warisan praktik dan gagasan artistiknya. 

—
Radi Arwinda (1983-2025) reflected on an ongoing journey of self-exploration between two cultures. His upbringing was deeply rooted in Sundanese culture. As he grew, global cultural influences began to enter his life, creating an identity conflict within himself.

Signifying a new chapter of his journey, Radi combines popular-cultural symbols with traditional ornamentation in his work. His artistic practice goes beyond superficial cultural appreciation, reflecting how local culture adapts in a fast-moving and unstable world.🔍👨‍🎨

His works are presented at ARTJOG as a tribute to Radi Arwinda, to carry on the legacy of his artistic practice and ideas.

🃏Radi Arwinda Experience, Ngulawang, 2026.

🚰💧 Sirin Farid Stevy (@faridstevy ) & Paseduluran Nandur Banyu (@daksina_arga ), Sumur Sinaba, 2026. 

Sirin Farid Stevy dan Paseduluran Nandur Banyu menanggapi isu pengelolaan air di Gunungkidul melalui karya instalasi kolaboratif. Mengangkat kontradiksi antara dua sumur simulasi, karya ini menyampaikan harapan dan kekhawatiran warga, sekaligus menekankan pentingnya melindungi sumber air yang bermakna secara ekologis, sosial, dan politik bagi kawasan tersebut.

Dalam Meet The Artist (20/08), Farid bercerita bahwa kerja fisik ini didorong oleh bakti kepada tanah kelahirannya. Kolektif ini pun memaparkan bagaimana sejak awal Juni, mereka telah membersihkan, memperbaiki, dan merawat kembali beberapa titik sumur. Catatannya lalu mereka tuangkan ke dalam booklet yang dibagikan kepada para peserta. 

Pertemuan ini berlanjut dalam “Sinau Ma(n)capat” pada petang hari. Mereka belajar membaca dan melagukan puisi tradisional Jawa sambil meresapi nilai tutur sebagai cara memulihkan ingatan kolektif dan upaya untuk bertahan hidup bersama. 

—
Sirin Farid Stevy and Paseduluran Nandur Banyu address water management issues in Gunungkidul through a collaborative installation. Highlighting the contradictions within two simulated wells, the work conveys residents’ hopes and fears while emphasizing the importance of protecting water sources, which hold ecological, social, and political meaning for the region.

During Meet The Artist (20/08), Farid shared that this physical labor stemmed from a desire to honor their homeland. The collective also described how, since early June, they had been cleaning, repairing, and restoring several wells. They later compiled their notes into a booklet and distributed it to the participants.

The evening continued with “Sinau Ma(n)capat”. They learned to read and chant Javanese tembang (traditional poetry), absorbing the oral wisdom of Javanese language and literature as a way to restore collective memory and navigate mutual survival.🌱

Catur Nugroho (@catur__nugroho ) secara kritis menanggapi perubahan lingkungan akibat pembangunan dan eksploitasi alam. 
Kepekaannya terhadap transformasi tersebut berakar dari pengalaman Catur tumbuh dan besar di Wonosobo, daerah pegunungan subur dengan sumber air melimpah di Jawa Tengah.⛰️

Dalam karyanya, ia menghadirkan pengalaman imersif yang paradoks melalui hamparan pasir, informasi tentang deforestasi, dan suara alam. Tanpa menyajikan solusi, Catur bertanya tentang apa saja yang masih terus dikorbankan, oleh siapa, dan apa yang akan diteruskan ke masa depan. Berpijak pada kosmologi Jawa, ia pun merefleksikan pentingnya harmoni antara manusia dan alam.

—
Catur Nugroho offers a critical perspective on the environmental changes caused by development and exploitation of natural resources. Growing up in Wonosobo, a mountainous region in Central Java known for its fertile soil and abundant water sources, influenced Catur’s sensitivity to these transformations. 

In his works, he creates a paradoxical, immersive experience through an expanse of sand, information on deforestation, and sounds of nature. Rather than providing clear solutions, Catur asks what continues to be sacrificed, by whom, and what will be left for future generations. Rooted in Javanese cosmology, he further reflects on the importance of harmony between humans and nature.🏜️

🏗️ Catur Nugroho, Lanskap Pasca-Peradaban (Post-Civilization Landscape), 2026.

Mula-mula, Annastasya Verina (@annastasyaver ) membawakan “Sebut Saja ‘n’” yang mengadaptasi ritme Nggandul dalam gamelan. Melalui artikulasi tubuhnya, ia mengajak kita melihat ulang arti ketepatan yang dibentuk oleh rasa dan konteks keseharian.

Suasana makin intens saat Yeni Wahyuni (@aenw__ ) x Rama A. (@anggaraarama ) & Haviz E. (@havizemriadi ) (IBBT @ibbt.institute ) mempresentasikan “Birth Code”. Lewat medium hibrida, mereka memetakan ulang budaya hari ini, menjadikan panggung sebagai cermin atas rapuhnya ruang hidup kita.🪞

—
How did intimacy fill the performa•ARTJOG x Bakti Budaya Djarum Foundation stage last night?

First, Annastasya Verina presented “Sebut Saja ‘n’”, drawing from the lingering pulse of Nggandul. Through her body articulation, she invited us to re-examine precision as something shaped by lived context and everyday feeling.🎭

The stage got more intense as Yeni Wahyuni x Rama A. & Haviz E. (IBBT) followed by “Birth Code”. Using a hybrid medium, they reinterpret contemporary culture, turning the stage into a reflection of increasingly fragile living conditions.

Aliansyah Caniago (@aliansyahcaniago ) dan Dani Huda (@danihuda ) mempresentasikan instalasi eksperimental berupa foto, film berdurasi tujuh menit, dan artefak pertunjukan dari hasil residensi mereka di Barus, Sumatra Utara. 

Selama residensi, keduanya menelusuri wilayah terdampak banjir 2025, sekaligus mendokumentasikan kondisi hidup dan kerugian warga setempat. Lewat karya ini, mereka menanggapi bencana alam sebagai babak baru dalam sejarah kolonisasi, perampasan tanah, dan industri ekstraktif di Sumatra.🪾

Resonansi karya ini diperluas melalui pertunjukan “Doa Untuk Jenggala” oleh Dani Huda dan Etza Meisyara (@etzameisyara ) kemarin (14/08). Memadukan narasi sinematik dengan pendekatan eksperimental dan olah bunyi eksperimental, pertunjukan ini mengajak pengunjung untuk sejenak berhenti, mendengarkan, serta memberikan penghormatan kepada alam semesta.

—
Aliansyah Caniago and Dani Huda present an experimental installation featuring photographs, a seven-minute film, and artifacts from performances stemming from their residency in Barus, North Sumatra. 

During their residency, the artists developed performances that documented sites affected by the catastrophic floods in 2025 and the living conditions and losses experienced by residents. Through this work, they respond to the disaster as part of a long history of colonization, land dispossession, and extractive industries in Sumatra.🌿

This work resonated further through a live sonic ritual “Doa Untuk Jenggala” (Prayer for the Forest) by Dani Huda and Etza Meisyara yesterday (14/08). Blending cinematic narratives and an experimental approach to sound, this performance invited us to pause, listen, and pay respect to the universe.

🍂Aliansyah Caniago X Dani Huda, Pulang Kampung, 2026.

Rainbow Disco Club 2026 に向けて4月4日(土) にプレパーティーを開催！今年はなんと20:00にオープンし、豪華ラインナップとともに朝まで駆け抜ける特別版となっている。

Caribou名義でワールドクラスの人気と実力を兼ね備えたDaphni がRDC 2026だけでなくプレパーティーにも出演。先日リリースした新アルバム「Butterfly」を引っ提げ、非常に貴重な3時間のオープニングセットを披露する。
また、RDC 2026 では Antal とのB2Bで出演する Hunee も登場。ソロでの国内出演は実に8年ぶり、この機会をお見逃しなく。さらに、アムステルダムが生んだ新たなスター Masalo が LIVE SET で本公演のみに出演することが決定。彼の特徴的なサウンドの中でもよりエレクトロニックな領域に踏み込んだダンサブルな LIVE SET は必見だ。
国内からは〈Rhythm Section〉や〈Animal Dancing〉など、名門レーベルから快作を連発している Mayurashka がメインフロアに登場する。

4F FLOOR にも2組の海外アーティストの招聘に成功。1組目は、ベトナムはホーチミンの名門クラブ The Observatory の創設者であり、同国におけるダンスミュージックの発展と繁栄を支える最重要人物 Hibiya Line が出演する。2組目はリスボンを拠点に活躍するDJ、ラジオパーソナリティのAnyaが初来日を果たす。Javybz としても活躍する彼女はNTS Radioで〈All Styles All Smiles with Javybz〉を毎月担当している。常に新しくて刺激的な音楽を探求し続けている彼女のセットは必見だ。

1F FLOOR には、南アフリカ発のダンスミュージック Amapiano を中心に、ヒップホップ、アフロビーツ、UKガレージなどをプレイするモンスターパーティー集団「AMAPINIGHT」がRDCに初登場。国内を代表する Amapiano の DJ として躍進しているMitokon や Ajuchan をはじめ、「AMAPINIGHT」クルーが総出で出演し1F FLOORを熱狂の渦に巻き込む。

Today, on National Sorry Day, we acknowledge the strength and resilience of the Stolen Generations, and reflect on the lasting impacts of Australia’s history for First Nations peoples and communities.
 
As we move into National Reconciliation Week tomorrow, this year’s theme, All In, reminds us that reconciliation requires ongoing commitment from all of us, through listening, learning, truth-telling and meaningful action.
 
The arts have always created space for stories that challenge, connect and inspire. They help us deepen understanding, share experiences and imagine more inclusive futures together.
 
As an arts community, being all in means continuing to support First Nations voices, creativity and leadership, while reflecting on our shared histories and the role we each play in reconciliation.
 
Because reconciliation isn’t a moment. It’s something we actively create together.

Syska La Veggie (@syskalaveggie ) bersama Sekolah Alam Penanggungan (SALAMAN - @sekolahalampenanggungan )menghadirkan instalasi tenda imersif yang menyoroti perubahan makna Gunung Penanggungan, dari simbol harmoni kosmik menjadi ruang konsumsi dan rekreasi. Gunung ini telah lama dianggap suci, menjadi pusat spiritual, serta menjadi rumah bagi ratusan situs arkeologi. Saat ini, Penanggungan menghadapi ancaman lingkungan yang serius akibat pendakian massal dan ekspansi industri ekstraktif. Karya ini mengajak kita merenungkan pentingnya gunung ini secara budaya dan ekologis, serta mendorong aktivisme terhadap isu-isu serupa.⛰️

SALAMAN sendiri diinisiasi pada 2024 oleh Syska La Veggie dan komunitas di sekitar Gunung Penanggungan, Mojokerto, Jawa Timur. Wadah pembelajaran komunitas ini berfokus pada pendidikan lingkungan dan sejarah melalui seni serta kegiatan di alam terbuka untuk membentuk generasi yang sadar ekologi dan budaya.

—
Syska La Veggie and Sekolah Alam Penanggungan (SALAMAN) present an immersive tent installation that highlights the shifting meaning of Mount Penanggungan. Once seen as a symbol of cosmic harmony, it has now transformed into a site of consumption and recreation. This mountain has long been considered sacred and serves as a spiritual center and site of archaeological discoveries. However, it now grapples with serious environmental challenges due to the surge in mass hiking and the expansion of extractive industries. This installation invites us to reflect on the cultural and ecological value of Mount Penanggungan while inspiring activism around similar issues.🌳

SALAMAN was initiated in 2024 by Syska La Veggie and communities surrounding Mount Penanggungan, Mojokerto, East Java. It serves as a community learning platform focused on environmental and history education through art and outdoor activities, aiming to foster a generation that is ecologically conscious and culturally engaged.

⛺ Syska La Veggie & Sekolah Alam Penanggungan, Ring of Pawitra, 2026.

Amin Taasha (@amintaasha ) merespons tantangan hidup sehari-hari di tengah dunia yang senantiasa berubah. Amin meminjam kelenturan otot kuda yang mencerminkan pola pikir adaptif sebagai kekuatan hidup, serta menunjukkan bagaimana humor membantu kita menjaga kewarasan. Dalam karyanya, figur-figur mitologis seperti iblis dapat dipahami sebagai representasi makhluk yang kehilangan sisi kemanusiaannya akibat gejolak politik, kepercayaan, dan konflik batin.

Menurut Amin, hidup ini layaknya mimpi, di mana pada akhirnya kita harus terbangun dan segalanya akan usai. Perspektif ini ia sampaikan dalam Meet The Artist kemarin (13/08). Kisahnya berlanjut dengan penjelasan tentang bunga marigold yang ia tebar dalam karyanya. Bunga ini adalah petunjuk agar kita tidak tersesat, sekaligus menjadi benang harapan bagi setiap kejutan yang menanti di tempat yang semestinya kita tuju.

—
Amin Taasha responds to the everyday challenges within the ever-changing world. Amin borrows the suppleness of a horse’s muscles, mirroring an adaptive mindset as a strength for living this life, and recognizing how humor can help us maintain our sanity. In his work, the mythological figures can be understood as representations of beings who are losing their humanity due to political, belief-system, and internal conflicts.

For Amin, life resembles a dream, one that we eventually must awaken from, as everything will come to an end. He shared this perspective during yesterday’s Meet The Artist (13/08). He then explained the marigolds in his works. These flowers serve as a guiding light, helping us navigate our paths, while also symbolizing threads of hope for the unexpected that awaits us in our destined places. 

🌼🪴Amin Taasha, The Long Exhale of The World, 2024–2026.

■Open Lounge
フェスの合間にひと息ついたり、音楽好き同士が自然につながれるコミュニティラウンジ。

ラウンジ内では、来場者のみなさんが参加できる体験型コンテンツもご用意しています。

Berawal dari studio Atreyu Moniaga (@atreyumoniaga ) di Rawa Buaya, Jakarta Barat, Atreyu Moniaga Project @atreyumoniaga.project (AMP) berkembang menjadi pusat komunitas dan inkubator bagi para seniman muda. Selama 13 tahun, AMP telah membina lebih dari 50 seniman melalui praktik yang tidak hanya mengasah kemampuan artistik, tetapi juga membangun karakter, ketahanan, dan semangat berkarya.🔥

Di ARTJOG 2026, AMP berkolaborasi dengan kurator Nindy Djani (@nindysm ) untuk menghadirkan karya 11 seniman alumni: WD Willy (@wd.willy ), Clasutta (@clasutta ), Liffi Wongso (@liffi_wongso ), Tusita Mangalani (@tusitamangalani ), Zita Nuella (@zitanuella ), Rapha Lisa (@rapha.lisa ), Ada Khansa (@ada.khansa ), Ansn Martin (@ansnmartin ), Red Maerra (@redmaerra ), Oddyendry (@oddyendry ), dan Wilhemus Willy (@wilhemuswilly ). Lewat presentasinya, AMP menelusuri linimasa perjalanan mereka sejak 2013, arsip capaian dan catatan berbagai proyek seni para alumni pasca-AMP, serta seri dokumenter yang menayangkan sepak terjang mereka di kancah seni Asia Tenggara.🌐

—
What began in Atreyu Moniaga’s West Jakarta studio has evolved into a thriving community hub and incubator for young artists: Atreyu Moniaga Project (AMP). For 13 years, AMP has nurtured more than 50 artists through a practice that sharpens their artistic development, while honing their character, grit, and integrity.

For ARTJOG 2026, AMP collaborates with curator Nindy Djani to showcase the works of 11 alumni artists: WD Willy, Clasutta, Liffi Wongso, Tusita Mangalani, Zita Nuella, Rapha Lisa, Ada Khansa, Ansn Martin, Red Maerra, Oddyendry, and Wilhemus Willy. This presentation maps out their artistic journey since 2013, featuring milestone archives, post-AMP project highlights, and a documentary series capturing their moves across the Southeast Asian art scene.💫

🎯Atreyu Moniaga Project, Liminal/Periphery: Beyond Borders, Beyond Possibilities, 2026.

Spektrum karya yang kontras bergantian hadir di panggung performa•ARTJOG x Bakti Budaya Djarum Foundation akhir pekan lalu. 

Artchipelago Dance Collective (@artchplg ) membawakan “Adeg” pada Sabtu (08/08) yang mengamati peristiwa kecil dan intim dalam tubuh, seperti napas yang tertahan dan langkah yang ragu-ragu, untuk mengajak kita menengok kembali pengalaman rapuh yang sering luput dari perhatian.🩰

Sementara pada malam berikutnya, Post Party Syndroma (@postpartysyndroma ) menghadirkan “Kiosk Chaos” yang berakar dari kerja pengarsipan daring budaya klub dan internet Indonesia sejak 2019, menghubungkan berbagai komunitas lewat proyek audiovisual, zine, label rekaman, hingga mode sebagai arsip yang dapat dikenakan.🪩

—
The performa•ARTJOG x Bakti Budaya Djarum Foundation stage featured two distinct performances over the weekend.

On Saturday (08/08), Artchipelago Dance Collective presented “Adeg”, observing small, intimate moments within the body, from a caught breath to a hesitant step, to invite us to notice the fragile experiences we so often overlook.🫁

On Sunday (09/08), Post Party Syndroma brought “Kiosk Chaos”. Rooted in their online archiving of Indonesian club and internet culture since 2019, their performance highlights cross-disciplinary connections through audiovisual projects, zines, record labels, and wearable merchandise as archives.🎛️

La historia del rock ha visto cosas muy extrañas. Pero apellidarse Beard (barba) en un grupo en el que el vello facial ha sido seña de identidad y ser el único que no la luce, es un caso de estudio. Eso sí, Frank Beard llevaba el boogie de Texas metido hasta lo más profundo de sus huesos, puro ritmo de blues aguardentoso y rock polvoriento. Hoy, el batería eterno de ZZ Top nos ha dejado a los 77 años. Tras la marcha de Dusty Hill en 2021, ya solo queda el emblemático Billy Gibbons del trío original que nos visitara en #bbklive en 2008 y unos años más tarde en #azkenarockfestival en 2015. Beard supo adaptarse igual al blues rezumante de gasolina y barro de los discos de los 70 del grupo como a su transformación en una maquinaria de rock ‘mainstream’ y grandes hits de los 80, y toda su ósmosis sonora posterior. Un auténtico titán de los tambores, al que tuvimos la suerte de ver en plena apoteosis rítmica. Descanse en paz.

Less than a month out from my first @lostandfoundbikeride!

After crashing my bike a couple weeks ago, I’ve been trying to take it easy to let my body recover and heal. Unfortunately, I only operate in extremes of lots of activity or no activity at all, and lately I’ve been a sloth. I am currently signed up for the Full Bull (99 miles with 6000~ feet of elevation gain) because my friends said it’s somehow easier than the Mid Moo…? It’s time to get my little butt into gear these next few weeks. 😬

Bike racing can be real expensive so I’ve got a handful of 10% off discount codes for @lostandfoundbikeride. Leave a comment, or send me a DM and I’ll get you a code that can be used on any of the distances.

The @lostandfoundbikeride is a fundraiser supporting @sierratrails’ Connected Communities project with the goal of connecting 15 mountain communities via singletrack, improving trail access and connectivity in order to strengthen the economies of rural communities, and encourage diverse user types to explore and recreate on public lands.

Elemen instalasi berupa kotak susu, rantai kain bermotif militer, gambar sepanjang 3,2 meter, hingga interaksi pengunjung lewat stiker semut, menyoroti bagaimana agenda politik meresap ke kehidupan sehari-hari.🧃🍱

Ia memaparkan proses kreatifnya dalam menjahit pengalaman pribadi menjadi kritik sosial, serta bagaimana praktik artistiknya memberikan perhatian pada realitas hubungan yang kompleks antara kebijakan pemerintah dan struktur sosial-politik dengan dorongan untuk bertahan hidup. 

—
Restu Ratnaningtyas responds to generational shifts through a critical highlight on public policy programs, notably “Free Nutritious Meals” (MBG). Elements like milk cartons, military-patterned fabric chains, a 3.2-meter drawing, and interactive ant stickers create a contemplative space that reflects how political agendas permeate everyday lives.🥛🪖

During yesterday’s Meet The Artist (06/08), she shared her perspective as a single mother, discussing her creative process of weaving personal experiences into social commentary. She then elaborated how her artistic practice highlights the complex relationship between broader socio-political structures and government policies, with the struggle for survival.

Praktik seni A. Sebastianus (@a.sebastianus ) mengeksplorasi hubungan dan pengalaman mendasar manusia dengan megalit, terutama dalam konteks sosial serta spiritual. Dalam karya ini, ia mengumpulkan berbagai benda peninggalan leluhurnya, termasuk pakaian, buku, dan mebel, yang kemudian ia kremasi dan gubah menjadi batu buatan. Ia melilit batu-batu tersebut dengan tali kain yang dicetak dari foto-foto keluarganya untuk melambangkan pelestarian tubuh, waktu, dan kosmologi. Melalui instalasi ini, A. Sebastianus menciptakan ritual baru tentang penghormatan dan meditasi terhadap ingatan dan pusaka dengan caranya sendiri.🪨

Pengalaman menikmati karya ini juga diperluas melalui site-responsive sound performance oleh Kinski Onggara (@kinski.kinski.kinski ), Jumat (07/08). Ia merespons material karya dengan merangkai rekamannya menjadi alunan suara yang terkikis secara bertahap untuk menggambarkan peluruhan bentuk dan identitas yang menyatu kembali ke asalnya.

—
A. Sebastianus’s artistic practice explores fundamental human relationships and experiences with megaliths, particularly within social and spiritual contexts. In this work, he collects family heirlooms like clothing, books, and furniture, which he then cremated and transformed into synthetic stones. He wraps these stones in a series of cords from fabric printed with images of his family photographs to symbolize the preservation of the body, time, and cosmology. Through this installation, A. Sebastianus creates a new ritual of reverence and meditation on memory and heritage in his own way.🏺 

The experience of the installation was further enriched through a site-responsive sound performance by Kinski Onggara on Friday (07/08). This performance interacted with the work’s materials, arranging their recordings into a soundscape that gradually degraded, reflecting the erosion of form and identity as they merge back into their origins.

🗿 A. Sebastianus, Tilas Waktu: Lithic Phenomenologies of Belonging, 2026.

Dita Gambiro (@ditagam ) merekonstruksi fasad ruko dan suasana kantor era 1990-an sebagai simulasi yang menghubungkan memori, ruang, arsitektur, dan trauma. Karya ini berangkat dari pengamatannya terhadap gedung-gedung terbengkalai di Jakarta, seperti Slipi, Kebayoran, Gajah Mada, dan Harmoni, rute yang kerap dilalui Dita semasa sekolah. 

Melalui eksplorasi spasial dan materialitas, Dita mengungkap bagaimana perubahan batasan psikologis dan sosial yang diakibatkan oleh trauma memengaruhi pembentukan identitas serta pergeseran sosial. Dalam Meet The Artist kemarin (06/08), Dita Gambiro juga menyampaikan pentingnya memori kolektif ini untuk mencegah tragedi serupa terulang di masa depan.🏬

—
Dita Gambiro reconstructs shopfront façades and a 1990s-style office space to create a simulation connecting memory, space, architecture, and trauma. This installation is inspired by her observations of abandoned buildings across Jakarta’s Slipi, Kebayoran, Gadjah Mada, and Harmoni areas, routes familiar to Dita during her school years. 

Through spatial and material exploration, Dita reveals how trauma imposes psychological and social boundaries that shape identity and social consciousness. During yesterday’s Meet The Artist (06/08), Dita Gambiro shared the importance of this collective memory to help prevent similar tragedies from occurring in the future.🏚️

This year we’re excited to include a 2.4-mile section of the Lake Davis Trail into all three Lost & Found courses, adding singletrack to the routes for the first time. This mellow, mostly smooth trail is perfect for drop bars—it winds through the woods at a nearly flat grade and is wide enough to pass (always let the rider in front of you know you’re passing). If you’ve joined the Friday Shakeout Ride in the past few years, you’ll recognize it! If not—head up to Lake Davis for the Shakeout Ride this year on Friday June 12 to check it out before race day! 

The non-motorized, beginner-friendly 7-mile Lake Davis Trail was built by race organizer Sierra Buttes Trail Stewardship in partnership with the Beckwourth District of the Plumas National Forest over many years, and with contributions from hundreds of volunteers, incorporating techniques such as turnpikes and boardwalks to prevent standing water during the wet season and promote longterm trail sustainability. Its beautiful lake views and beginner-friendly status make it a real gem and we’re thrilled to showcase it in this year’s race on Saturday, June 13. 

Participating in races like Lost & Found helps us keep doing this kind of work, as all proceeds from the race benefit the Stewardship. Your race entry=support for trails! 

Find all the details on the all-new 2026 race courses (40, 58 & 99 miles), links to race registration and the RSVP for the Friday ride at lostandfoundbikeride.com. A @gravelearthseries event, presented by @evilbicycles

さらに、Love InternationalやGlastonburyの象徴的ステージ「Silver Hayes」をキュレーションするDave Harveyも登場。ハウス、エレクトロ、EBM、時にはスロートラックまで、多彩な音楽を独自の感性で束ねるUKダンスミュージックの革新者の一人だ。そしてRainbow Disco Clubからは、7月開催のLove International本祭への出演も決定しているレジデントDJ、Sisiが参加する。ティスノの祝祭感と渋谷の夜が交差する、歴史的な一夜をお見逃しなく。

16/100.  In the Spring of 2022, the world decided it was a good time to come to the United States for the first form of a “Tour” since the Covid-19 Pandemic. 

Despite only being two events, this month-long rip was one of the most potent periods of skating I’ve ever been around. 

Here, we had one of the best Maryhill Freerides and Races to date, with the “Tour De Maryhill” being the last leg of the tour.  With Australians, Europeans, South Americans and more, it felt like a glimpse into the Maryhills of years past. Max Capps won the race, everyone had a great time (for the most part 😂), and then we all decided to go back to NC to put down gnarly runs on the craziest hills in North America.

Over the next week or two, I will be going back in reverse-chronological order of the different events I’ve shot over the years.  From there, I will share some stories of legendary sessions such as the NC sessions I mentioned above. Any feedback or requests are welcomed. I hope you enjoy this trip down memory lane.

Cheers!

June 13, 2026. Lost and Found is back in Portola for its 13th edition, and it’s back for the second year in a row as part of the Gravel Earth Series.

Lost Sierra gravel is simple and honest. Long roads, dust, pine trees, quiet miles and enough space to ride at your own rhythm. Some will push. Others will just settle in and enjoy the day. Both belong here.

Portola doesn’t feel like a venue. It feels like a town opening its doors. Locals cheering, food waiting at the finish, music in the background, riders sitting on the ground talking about their day.

Signing up also means supporting the place you ride through. The event gives back to @sierratrails Sierra Buttes Trail Stewardship, helping keep these trails open, connected and cared for.

🧭 Good to know: save something for the second half. Lost and Found has a way of asking for patience.

🗣2026 Route Announcement! 

The new Lost and Found Gravel routes are here for 2026, with more dirt, a better finish and singletrack! All three routes will now a stretch of the SBTS-built singletrack Lake Davis Trail (if you’ve participated in the Friday Shakeout Ride in recent years, you’ll know it—super fun, flowy and fast & perfect for gravel bikes). We’ll also use parts of the Beckwourth-Gennessee and 24N10 roads to add in beautiful riding around Lake Davis (big thanks to our longstanding partners Plumas National Forest, Beckwourth Ranger District, the city of Portola and Plumas County Roads Department for the close work on the new routes!). Otherwise, you can expect the usual mix of smooth, fast gravel to chunky Lost Sierra dirt roads—and the race will feature a brand-new finish to cut out the final headwind-filled, pavement miles. The distances are the roughly same: 99, 58 and 40 miles, with a slightly less elevation gain from last year and more dirt. The Full Bull is 84% dirt, the Mid Moo is 70% and the Half Calf is 60%, so plan your set-up accordingly. 

EARLY BIRD REGISTRATION IS OPEN until 12/31, offering a 10 % discount on the entry fee and a new race cancellation policy. Find all the race and route details at lostandfoundbikeride.com, and we’ll see you next June 13th in Portola for another epically beautiful weekend in the Lost Sierra! Lost & Found is part of the @gravelearthseries in 2026.

Did you know there’s a way to race all of the SBTS events without paying an entry fee? We try hard to keep our fees consistent each year while still offering an awesome race experience, but we know it’s expensive to commit to a full race weekend. That’s where our Peer to Peer Fundraising program comes in—if you raise double the amount you paid in entry fees before race day, we’ll credit you the original fee you paid back to your credit card. We’ll also have someone from our staff help you craft messaging that speaks to why you want to fundraise on behalf of Sierra Buttes Trail Stewardship, provide any images you need and walk you through the best ways to reach your network with that message. It’s a great way to contribute more dollars to the SBTS mission, while helping you shoulder the financial burden of racing. If you want more details, or want to sign up to fundraise, drop us a DM or email gina@sierratrails.org.

‘One Step Beyond’ the rest, Madness have been making hits and mischief for 45 years. Choose dancing on the grass after sunset. Choose the long weekend over work on Monday. Choose Underworld.

Thirty years ago, the dancefloor changed. At the turn of the decade, acid house opened the door to a new UK rave scene – where indie heads joined the club crowds and transformed empty fields and derelict warehouses into spaces of community and transcendence. And in 1994, Underworld emerged onto the scene with their third album ‘dubnobasswithmyheadman’. 

Their visionary and uninhibited approach to dance music soon caught the attention of director Danny Boyle, landing the group on the soundtrack of the seminal 1996 film Trainspotting with the generation-defining single ‘Born Slippy .NUXX’. Now, Underworld return to the cultural zeitgeist, and to Adelaide for the first time since 2010 for what will be an unmissable set at WOMADelaide on Friday 5 March.

The 2026 winner of the @InspiringSouthAustralia Science in Art Award is: @Chris_Boha_Art!

Chris’s incredibly detailed three-dimensional layered work demonstrated a high level of skill and sincere engagement with climate science. The judging panel were impressed by the considered approach the artist took with both the construction of the work and the conceptual underpinnings of the work.

📍 11am Saturday 29 August 2026, at Wombat Workshop in Semaphore.
🎟️ $185+BF via the link in our bio (includes infrared film, materials, equipment, and lunch.)

This workshop is supported by @InspiringSouthAustralia, which provides South Australians with opportunities to connect with, be involved in and get excited about science, technology, engineering and maths (STEM).

The 2026 winner of the @DonDunstanFoundation Award is: Bianca Joanna Buliga! @BiancaJoannaPhotography

Bianca’s series of photographic self portraits were technically accomplished and deeply emotive.

The judges felt that the artist took a difficult subject -that could be hard for the public to access- and approached it with generosity and empathy. It was introspective, but the overwhelming feeling was one of inclusion – opening a door for other people to feel seen.

The judges were impressed by the high degree of skill and ever-evolving nature of Soeffky’s work across the festival. This was an evolving work, which each judge visited at a different stage over the course of the festival. It was clear to the panel that this artist is evolving their practice in an exciting, multidisciplinary direction with the confidence to move beyond conventions of artmaking.

At the closing day, one judge described Soeffky’s exhibition as feeling like they had “arrived at the end of a hell of a party”, and all of the judges were left feeling that they absolutely want to be invited to the next one.

@LauraFrancesWills has added some new A3 prints to @ShopSALA.com.au to celebrate the 'Shore Lines' project which can be enjoyed this weekend in Port Adelaide as part of the River Night Walk.

The first artwork pictured above, 'Portrait of a Boy as a Mangrove', stemmed from a creative research project about mangroves and features Wills' signature use of a map within the work. 

"In 2020 the mangrove woodland that grows in Adelaide's northern shores experienced a huge dieback. The St Kilda Mangroves Alliance formed to ensure best practice for their remediation in this globally significant area. Through the tidal salty water you can see a half boy-half mangrove tree drawn into a map of Adelaide."

THE BREAKFAST CLUB EASTER CELEBRATION | A SUBTLE THOUGHT EXPERIMENT FOR ALL YOU TRUE BELIEVERS
—
Let’s, for a second, imagine one thing we truly value.
Our friends. Our partners. Our family. Our EU thrifted red horse leather flares that fit perfectly right on the hips perhaps.
—
Now let’s imagine that whatever that thing is, all of a sudden it gets taken away from us
—
It’s gone
It was there for a moment, but now it’s not
And it ain’t ever truly coming back
—
Would we appreciate it more?
Or would we appreciate it less?
—
What is our relationship with loss?
Is loss a negative?
Or is it the thing that gives value its shape?
—
Because maybe it is only in losing something that we realise what it was worth
—
So what do we celebrate?
The thing itself?
Or the fact that its loss is what made it matter in the first place?
—
At BC, we take Easter as a time to ask questions like these
—
What is truly worth celebrating?
The thing? The loss? Or the return?
—
Doors from 22:00 rolling right through to Tuesday morning, let’s find out together

Artisan Series • Natalija Rushidi | @natalijarushidi ✂️✨

Natalija Rushidi creates fashion shaped by philosophy, not trend. Born in Serbia and now based in Sydney, she launched her label from a frustration with fast, wasteful fashion and its disconnect from the wearer. What began as resistance evolved into intention - small collections that are handmade, beautifully constructed and always slightly unexpected.

Her work is defined by architectural silhouettes, conceptual foundations and disciplined restraint. Structure and sensuality coexist. Strength and softness sit side by side. 🔥

Most pieces are produced in her studio-store, reinforcing a commitment to quality over quantity and ethical, considered production. Rather than chasing cycles, Natalija builds collections around ideas - garments designed to endure beyond seasons.

Her client is thoughtful and expressive. She values alignment over excess. She chooses pieces that elevate rather than overwhelm. What excites Natalija most is transformation. Watching a woman stand taller when she feels aligned with what she’s wearing is, in her words, “incredibly powerful.” 🙌

Inspired by art, architecture and women themselves - their complexity, duality and presence - she continues to design with intention rather than impulse.

“What I love about The Big Design Market is the opportunity it brings to meet people who value craftsmanship and intention.”

Designed with conviction. Constructed with precision. Worn with confidence. 💫

DSAF26 ARTIST: Katie Hagebols aka @piperkidd_ is a Darwin based artist living on Larrakia Country. For over ten years in the Northern Territory, Katie has been inspired by her surroundings of remarkable landscapes and culture. Katie explores themes of acrylic on canvas abstract landscapes, river systems and maps along with dabbling in fine line work in the form of figurative drawings. Over the years, bright and bold colours have shone through Katie’s work, expressive of her personality, taking form in surreal portraits and motifs. In recent years, Katie has been more inclined to experimenting with new media, such as digital drawings through her new found love of Pro Create and rekindling her love of photography. Tales told by her favourite bushies and remote adventures fuel the never ending fire of portraying stories through her artworks. 

DSAF26: MAY 22 - JUNE 5

🎥 “La tecnología nos permite probar muchas cosas que antes ni siquiera podíamos imaginar.”

Hablamos con @andreiwarren, fundador y director creativo de @misatostudio, sobre cómo el 3D, la tecnología y la narrativa visual han transformado nuestra manera de crear.

Formado en Bellas Artes, Warren empezó a explorar la tecnología 3D como una forma de materializar ideas sin grandes recursos, convirtiendo las herramientas digitales y los tutoriales de YouTube en su propio espacio de experimentación creativa.

El creativo fue uno de los ponentes destacados de la última edición de @offfest en el DHub, donde describió la tecnología como una herramienta para acelerar procesos, abrir posibilidades creativas y repensar la manera de construir imágenes y narrativas visuales.
__

🎥 “Technology allows us to try many things we couldn’t even dream of before.”

We spoke with @andreiwarren, founder and creative director of @misatostudio, about how 3D, technology and visual storytelling have transformed the way we create.

With a Fine Arts background, Warren turned to 3D technology, digital tools and YouTube tutorials to bring ideas to life through creative experimentation.

The creative was one of the featured speakers at the latest edition of @offfest at DHub, where he described technology as a tool to accelerate processes, unlock creative possibilities, and rethink the way images and visual narratives are built.

📸 “L’art és capaç de desafiar allò que fa la tecnologia, i la tecnologia pot inspirar allò que fa l’art.”

Parlem amb l’artista visual i fòtograf Reuben Wu (@reuben) sobre els límits entre art, tecnologia i experimentació visual. Després de treballar com a músic durant molt de temps, la fotografia es va convertir en el seu llenguatge creatiu. Avui, els seus projectes capten les manifestacions artístiques dels fenòmens naturals utilitzant innovacions tecnològiques.

En una entrevista durant l’última edició de l’@offfest al DHub, Wu reflexiona sobre com la tecnologia no només transforma les eines creatives, sinó també la manera d’imaginar i construir noves narratives visuals.
 __

📸 “El arte es capaz de desafiar aquello que hace la tecnología, y la tecnología puede inspirar aquello que hace el arte.”

Hablamos con el artista visual y fotógrafo Reuben Wu (@reuben) sobre los límites entre el arte, la tecnología y la experimentación visual. Después de trabajar durante mucho tiempo como músico, la fotografía se convirtió en su lenguaje creativo. Hoy, sus proyectos capturan las manifestaciones artísticas de los fenómenos naturales utilizando innovaciones tecnológicas.

En una entrevista durante la última edición de OFFF Festival en el Disseny Hub Barcelona, Wu reflexiona sobre cómo la tecnología no solo transforma las herramientas creativas, sino también la manera de imaginar y construir nuevas narrativas visuales.
__

📸 “Art is capable of challenging what technology does, and technology can inspire what art does.”

We spoke with visual artist and photographer Reuben Wu (@reuben) about the boundaries between art, technology, and visual experimentation. After working as a musician for many years, photography became his creative language. Today, his projects capture the artistic manifestations of natural phenomena through technological innovation.

In an interview during the latest edition of OFFF Festival at Disseny Hub Barcelona, Wu reflects on how technology not only transforms creative tools, but also the way we imagine and build new visual narratives.

DSAF26 ARTIST: @sofles is an Australian graffiti artist originating from Brisbane. Self-taught, he has been honing his skills for over 20 years, exploring various mediums such as spraypaint, acrylic, drawing and brush painting, as well as digital and illustration works. Sofles’ large scale murals have taken him around the world ten times over and now grace many of the world’s largest cities, including Berlin, Copenhagen, Oslo, Las Vegas, and LA… and one of Darwin’s most iconic walls: the Austin Lane mud crab. 

Sofles has a clear goal with his art; he aims to create strong images that evoke emotions in people. Drawing inspiration from nature, society, graffiti and traditional art, his work focuses on the ideas of time, dimensions, and an abstract mix of past experiences.

We can’t wait to welcome Sofles back to the streets of Darwin 🔥

Artisan Series • Darragh Murphy | @marlowoodwork 🪵✨ Marlo Woodwork is an Australian design studio creating sculptural lighting and furniture shaped by nature, craftsmanship and time. Grounded in slow making and sustainable practice, each piece is designed to live beautifully in a home, as both a functional object and a work of art.

Marlo began from a desire to slow down and create something lasting. After years in fast-paced environments, the founders relocated from Sydney to Tasmania for a few years, drawn by its raw beauty and the opportunity to build something meaningful by hand. What began as experiments in steam bending evolved into a collection inspired by Tasmania’s striking locations, from the Amos floor lamp to the Elysia wall light and Tullah coat rack.

At the heart of the practice is patience. Steam bending, shaping timber with heat, water and time, demands calm, care and precision, resulting in organic forms that simply can’t be rushed or replicated.

Every piece is sculptural yet made to be used. Pendant lights transform a room through shadow play, coat racks double as wall sculpture. Material honesty is central, with timbers sourced through sustainable practices, from recovered Tasmanian blackwood to responsibly stewarded oak. 🔥〰️

The most exciting moment? Watching timber begin to bend. Feeling the fibres shift, hearing the wood take its new shape and seeing an idea inspired by nature come to life through your hands. It’s this process that allows each piece to carry both permanence and poetry.

Creatively, Marlo draws inspiration from Tasmania’s wild edges where land meets water. Shorelines, ripples and shifting light are reflected in designs like the Amos pendant.

“The Big Design Market brings together people who truly appreciate craft and story. It’s a chance to connect, to have meaningful conversations, and to feel part of a community that values sustainability, quality and design with purpose.”

Sculptural, slow and shaped by nature, Marlo Woodwork creates lighting and furniture designed to be lived with for generations. 💫👏

🎨💜 For this year’s edition of @creativelunchclub at @offfest we did a super cool collaboration with Brazilian artist @marinaesmeraldo.

She hand painted a 6m long table cloth for our table, where 20 creatives enjoyed lunch together on each of the three festival days.

The inspiration? Spain’s beautiful tradition of sobremesa. The word literally means „upon the table“ and refers to the art of lingering long after a meal ends, time set aside for conversation, storytelling, and simply enjoying each other’s company. For Spaniards, dining is far more than satisfying hunger. It’s a shared experience, a moment to pause and connect.

We wanted to bring that spirit to OFFFest: a long table, a hand-painted cloth full of life and color, and a group of creatives. Just food, ideas, and good conversation flowing freely.

Video by @juanislasss / @weekndr.tv

Artisan Series • Ben Thompson | @charliemiddletonsyd 🪡✂️

Charlie Middleton began as a gradual evolution rather than a single defining moment. In the early 2000s, Ben Thompson set out to start a clothing label with no formal training - just instinct and determination. A few years in, wanting to make himself a belt, he took a small Saturday leather class. That first belt turned out beautifully, and something clicked. 👜✨ 

With no YouTube tutorials to guide him, Ben taught himself through trial and error -learning by doing, refining by hand. Having trained as a carpenter after school, his understanding of structure and material translated seamlessly into working with firm vegetable-tanned leathers. What began as a small addition to the label quickly became central to it.

In 2006, after persistent requests for softer waist belts, Ben designed his first soft leather style. It marked a shift in direction and the birth of Charlie Middleton as its own brand. By 2010, with new equipment and a larger workshop, he began handcrafting bags - a slow, self-taught process that shaped the brand’s clean, understated aesthetic. 🔥

At the heart of Charlie Middleton is an uncompromising commitment to quality. Ben personally selects every hide and hand-cuts each panel for every bag - a time-intensive approach that allows the use of exceptional leathers rarely seen in mass production. 🙌

Simplicity defines the designs, allowing material and craftsmanship to take centre stage. And because each bag is individually made, customers can customise from over 50 leathers, hardware options and linings, creating something truly personal. 🤎

“The Big Design Market visitors are incredibly savvy at spotting quality,” Ben shares. “The response has always been really special.”

Built slowly, shaped by hand and driven by a passion for making things well, Charlie Middleton is craftsmanship in its purest form. 💫

DSAF26 ARTIST: Tom Gerrard is an Australian painter whose works focus on his personal environment. His style developed through his prolific international output on the streets, and he incorporates contemporary techniques in his work such as spray paint and airbrush. 
Gerrard’s works compress space through bold flattened colour schemes, employing a signature black outline which frames his graphical forms. Observation is key to Gerrard’s practice; the architectural elements and domestic objects are taken directly from his environment, both at home and through travel. Gerrard has exhibited in Los Angeles, Barcelona and Tokyo, and his works have been acquired by the National Gallery of Australia and the National Gallery of Victoria. He is an active international muralist, having been commissioned in London, Berlin, Quito, Mumbai and Rio de Janeiro.

DSAF26 ARTIST: @george_rose is an Australian artist and painter working internationally transitioning between Australia and Europe. She is known for her distinctive style, large-scale murals and colour-driven works.
Her use of surreal colour palettes, transitional gradients and detailed linework interrogates how symbols, especially floral ones, accrue meaning. Her work reflects on her relationship with memory, visual classification and the decorative. Drawing from a decade-long archive of photographed botanicals and through self-driven research, she sketches and collages elements. She uses colour, negative space and shifts in scale to create botanical and abstract forms that function as allegorical imagery, intentionally disconnecting from narrative-driven representation.
Drawing is central to her practice, forming the foundation of her work. Graphic and organic forms create tension between the figurative and the abstract, challenging associations between the ornament, the botanical and the feminine.

DSAF26 artist: Law graduate turned street artist @kaffeinepaints, paints public artwork globally, while pursuing realist portraiture in the studio. Combining creativity with a strong social conscience, her art projects invite audiences to engage with societal and political issues in unique ways.

Kaff-eine was the first female Australian artist to paint portraits on old grain silos for Australia’s iconic Silo Art Trail, and the first Australasian artist to create a pyrotechnic sculpture for Mexico’s international fireworks festival.

Kaff-eine is currently running her Yu Stories project; a youth-led, film and music storytelling initiative with Warlpiri youth in Yuendumu, supported by Wanta Aboriginal Corporation and the Central Land Council. 

She is also in the process of building her studio retreat on a Queensland island, in which artists can undertake residencies and research surrounded by Ramsar-protected wetlands.

Kaff is interested in further developing her solo murals as a storytelling medium; collaborating with more communities to create unique murals and projects that increase pride in place and identity; and continuing to work with creative thinkers in the Northern Territory, which she loves and considers her second home. 🫶

Kelas Aktivisme Seni (@kelas.aktivismeseni ) mempertemukan arsip dan karya baru dari 16 alumninya dalam sebuah karya kolaboratif yang disatukan dengan semangat Aksi Kamisan. Payung-payung hitam yang melayang di ruang pamer menjadi simbol perjuangan untuk keadilan, sementara karya dan arsip di bawahnya menunjukkan bagaimana praktik seni berpaut dengan keterlibatannya terhadap isu-isu budaya, politik, dan ketidakadilan di masyarakat.✊

Kelas Aktivisme Seni diperkenalkan oleh Dolorosa Sinaga (@dolorosasinaga ) pada 2014 sebagai mata kuliah pertama di Indonesia yang membahas persilangan antara seni dan aktivisme. Percakapan dalam Meet The Artist kemarin (30/07) menghadirkan 2 perwakilan, yaitu Bagus Purwoadi (@baguspurwoadi ) dan Nirwan Sambudi (@nirwansambudi ). Mereka berbagi proses kolaborasi di balik karya ini sekaligus mendiskusikan ekspresi sikap etis serta partisipasi aktif mereka dalam mengubah keyakinan tersebut menjadi tindakan.

—
Kelas Aktivisme Seni (Art Activism Class) presents a collaborative project featuring archival materials and new works from 16 of its alumni, inspired by the spirit of “Aksi Kamisan”. The floating black umbrellas symbolize the resilient struggle for justice, while the artworks and archives beneath them show how artistic practices can engage deeply with critical cultural, political, and social issues.⚖️

Introduced in 2014 by Dolorosa Sinaga, the Art Activism Class was Indonesia’s first university course dedicated to the intersections of art and activism. During Meet The Artist (30/07), two alumni, Bagus Purwoadi and Nirwan Sambudi, shared insights into their collaborative process. They discussed the ethical stances they uphold as artists and how they actively work to translate those beliefs into meaningful action.

☂️ Dolorosa Sinaga & Kelas Aktivisme Seni, Monumen Pembangkangan Sipil, 2026.

Nona Yoanishara (@nonaysarah ) melihat otak sebagai sistem yang terus-menerus diorganisasi ulang oleh pengalaman, termasuk trauma. Berangkat dari konsep ‘neuroplasticity’, karya ini menelusuri trauma sebagai proses yang perlahan menata ulang cara manusia mengalami dunia serta membentuk persepsinya terhadap ruang, tubuh, dan realitas. Instalasi ini mempertemukan visual kosmik, data gelombang otak, sinyal elektronik, dan atmosfer seperti transmisi yang terputus untuk menggambarkan bagaimana pengalaman traumatis dapat meninggalkan jejak yang terus memengaruhi sistem saraf.🧠

—
Nona Yoanishara views the brain as a system constantly reorganized by our experiences. Drawing from the concept of ‘neuroplasticity’, the work explores trauma as an ongoing condition that alters our perception of the world, space, the body, and reality. The installation combines cosmic imagery, brainwave data, electronic signals, and an atmosphere that feels like a disrupted transmission to explore how traumatic experiences can leave lasting traces within the nervous system.📡

📟 Nona Yoanishara, Post-Traumatic ‘Space’ Disorder, 2026.

A descendant of the Jawoyn people from the Northern Territory and of Irish ancestry, Baylis’ multi-faceted artistic practice is founded in the process of ‘queering’ and unsettling ‘traditional’ ways of representing Aboriginality. 
 
You may have seen his work from The @guildhouse_au Fellowship at @Agsa.adelaide during SALA Festival 2020 -we're still talking about all that glomesh! Troy-Anthony is pictured here with a remixed presentation of another work you might recognise from 2020, 'Tell Them Their Dreaming', which is currently on display across the entire facade of @WollongongArtGallery.
 
We can’t wait to chat to Troy-Anthony for an episode of the SALA Podcast, and get our hands on the @WakefieldPress book about his practice due for release this year! @CreateSA_

Karya ini berangkat dari perjumpaannya dengan Cucu Ayu, seorang penari Bajidoran (pertunjukan rakyat dari Jawa Barat). Were you with us at the performa•ARTJOG x Bakti Budaya Djarum Foundation stage?🌆

On Friday (31/07), Ahmad Susantri presented “Tetuha Halimawong”, drawing from his journey as a dancer, his experience of embracing his identity as a feminine man, and his decision to return to his hometown to teach dance to schoolchildren as a way of passing that knowledge on to the next generation.🕺🏻

The following evening, Saturday (01/08), Ela Mutiara presented “Pukau Penggerak Zaman: Nomor Persiapan, Pencekalan, dan Saweran”, rooted in her encounter with Cucu Ayu, a Bajidoran dancer (traditional dance from West Java). Through gesture, correction, pause, and misunderstanding, Ela traces how the body records presence and endurance as fragments of knowledge.

🏛️ “Cultural Collisions Goes Indonesia: When Heritage, Art, Stories and Generations Meet” membahas bagaimana mengomunikasikan makna budaya melalui pendekatan kreatif dan kolaboratif. 

Berdasarkan kerja sama selama lebih dari dua puluh tahun antara Austria dan Indonesia, para pembicara memaparkan kolaborasi interdisipliner di balik proyek tersebut untuk mengeksplorasi bagaimana gagasan yang kompleks dapat dipahami dengan lebih mudah, lebih nyata, dan lebih bermakna secara pribadi, termasuk bagi anak-anak. Proses ini mencakup menerjemahkan makna Sumbu Filosofi Yogyakarta sebagai poros budaya yang menghubungkan Gunung Merapi, Keraton Yogyakarta, dan Laut Selatan, serta menghadirkan cara baru bagi publik untuk mengalami Warisan Budaya Dunia.

—
“Cultural Collisions Goes Indonesia: When Heritage, Art, Stories and Generations Meet” highlighted how cultural meanings can be communicated through a creative and collaborative approach.

Building on over twenty years of partnership between Austria and Indonesia, the speakers shared the interdisciplinary efforts that drove the project, demonstrating how complex ideas can be made accessible, tangible, and personally significant, even for children. This journey includes translating the philosophical concept of the Yogyakarta Philosophical Axis (the cultural axis connecting Mount Merapi, the Yogyakarta Palace, and the Indian Ocean) into innovative ways for the public to engage with World Heritage.🧭

Pengalaman manusia hadir dalam bentuk fragmen-fragmen tindakan, peristiwa, dan situasi yang terus berulang dalam kehidupan sehari-hari. Seiring waktu, pengulangan tersebut membentuk kebiasaan, cara berpikir, serta cara kita memahami apa yang dianggap wajar.🔵

Dalam praktik seninya, Muhammad Yakin (@mmmyakin ) mengeksplorasi “zona abu-abu” dengan menciptakan figur-figur antropomorfik yang ditempatkan di atas latar belakang yang kompleks dan berlapis-lapis. Repetisi ini hadir dalam karyanya di ARTJOG 2026 untuk menggambarkan cara manusia memaknai waktu, identitas, dan kebebasan di dunia.

—

Human experience is shaped through fragments of actions, events, and situations that we encounter repeatedly in everyday life. Over time, this repetition forms habits, patterns of thought, and influences how we understand what is considered normal.

His practice grows from observations of what he refers to as the “gray area”, creating anthropomorphic figures set against intricate, layered backgrounds. Through his work for ARTJOG 2026, this focus on repetition becomes a way to depict how humans perceive time, identity, and freedom.🌀

Eko Nugroho (@ekonugroho_studio ) bersama empat alumni Versus Project (@versusxproject ), yaitu Dyah Retno Fitriani (@devetroo ), Febri Anugerah (@febrianugerah ), Aphrodita ‘Cemprut’ Wibowo (@cemprut ), dan Gindringwasted (@gindringwasted ), mengeksplorasi janji sebagai komitmen, pengakuan, sekaligus harapan yang tidak selalu terwujud. Dalam konteks sosial, janji dapat menjadi instrumen politik untuk memperoleh dukungan publik. Di sisi lain, janji juga hadir sebagai aspirasi pribadi yang ingin dicapai. Karya kolaboratif ini membuka berbagai kemungkinan terhadap realitas yang penuh harapan sekaligus penuh ketidakpastian.🎭

—
Eko Nugroho and four alumni of the Versus Project: Dyah Retno Fitriani, Febri Anugerah, Aphrodita ‘Cemprut’ Wibowo, and Gindringwasted presents the idea of promises as commitments, declarations, and sources of hope that are not always fulfilled. In a social context, promises are often used as political instruments to gain public support. At the same time, they can also represent personal aspirations that one hopes to achieve. Collectively, they invite us to explore different perspectives on a reality shaped by both hope and uncertainty.

🎪 Eko Nugroho & Versus Project, SIRKUS JANJI, 2026.

The book “Ditanggoeng Tida Loentoer” is based on archival research and collection efforts that began in 2010, documenting 502 visual cultural artifacts from 87 cities across 22 provinces in Indonesia. 

During the book discussion and launch on Monday (27/07), speakers and participants engage in meaningful exchanges on how these artifacts provide insights into Indonesia’s history through everyday objects that have subtly preserved its narrative.

TEMPA (@_tempa_ ) menghadirkan instalasi yang terdiri dari 25 laci serta rangkaian lukisan akrilik di atas kain kulit kayu Sinjulo sebagai upaya untuk menemukan kesadaran ruang situasional dalam memahami sejarah panjang manusia. Karya ini merupakan hasil riset artistik dan eksplorasi material sebagai medium refleksi untuk membaca hubungan kompleks antara manusia, tanah, memori, dan sistem nilai yang perlahan terkikis oleh logika komoditas modern.🍂

Dalam Meet The Artist kemarin (30/07), TEMPA berbagi cerita tentang perjalanan mereka ke Palu, Sulawesi Tengah, yang menjadi titik awal pembuatan karya ini. Bagi Rara, salah satu anggota TEMPA yang memiliki garis keturunan suku Kaili, perjalanan tersebut menjadi upaya untuk menjalin kembali koneksi emosional dengan tanah leluhur yang selama ini hidup dalam memori kolektif keluarganya. 

TEMPA, diinisiasi pada tahun 2015, terdiri atas Putud Utama (@putud.utama ) dan Rara Kuastra (@rarakuastra ).

—
TEMPA presents an installation of 25 drawers and a series of acrylic paintings on Sinjulo bark cloth to reflect on reality and cultivate spatial and situational awareness in understanding humanity’s long history. This work is an artistic research project and material exploration as a medium for reflecting on the complex relationships among humans, land, memory, and systems of values that are gradually being undermined by the pressures of modern commodification.🪵

During yesterday’s Meet The Artist (30/07), TEMPA shared their journey to Palu, Central Sulawesi, which became the starting point for creating this work. For Rara, a member of TEMPA and an artist of Kaili descent, this trip became an effort to reconnect with her ancestral roots, which have long been part of her family’s collective memory.

TEMPA, established in 2015, was founded by Putud Utama and Rara Kuastra.

Bagi Kunting, kursi yang kehilangan satu kaki menggambarkan rapuhnya kekuasaan, sementara batu menjadi beban ketidakadilan yang terus dibawa. —
Fj Kunting unpacked the ideas behind “Sit Seat Shit” during yesterday’s (23/07) Meet The Artist. For Kunting, the missing chair leg reflects the fragility of power, while the stone embodies the weight of injustice carried through everyday life. By removing the boundaries of the stage, the work sparks conversations about democracy’s fragility, the hidden labor behind power, and the physical reality of resistance. It continues to unfold through the conversations that spread across social media until today.🪨

Hanafi (@studio_hanafiart )berkolaborasi dengan tiga alumni residensi Galerikertas (@galerikertas.art ), yaitu Ajiba (@a1.jiba ), Asmoadji (@asmobewok ), dan David Bakti (@davidbaktiii ) untuk membayangkan regenerasi artistik sebagai proses “penempaan” yang terus berlangsung dan tak lekang oleh waktu. Berpusat pada material tembaga yang melipat ke dalam dirinya sendiri, karya kolaboratif mereka melambangkan pertemuan masa lalu dan masa depan dalam “gulungan waktu” yang dibentuk oleh banyak tangan. Seperti proses menempa logam, hubungan antargenerasi dipahami sebagai proses saling membentuk, bertahan, dan membuka ruang bagi kebebasan berekspresi.⛓️

—
Hanafi collaborated with three Galerikertas residency alumni, who are Ajiba, Asmoadji, and David Bakti, to envision an artistic regeneration as a “forging” process that is timeless and enduring beyond time’s limits. Centered on sheets of copper folded inward upon themselves, this work symbolizes the encounter between the past and the future like a “roll of time” formed by many hands. Like the act of forging metal, intergenerational relationships are understood as a process of shaping one another, enduring change, and making space for artistic freedom.🔶

🔨 Hanafi & Galerikertas: Ajiba, Asmoadji, dan David Bakti, Menempa dan Ditempa, 2026.

Two dance performances moved the audience at the performa•ARTJOG x Bakti Budaya Djarum Foundation stage.

Last night (25/07), Muslimin Bagus Pranowo presented “1518”, inspired by the 1518 Dancing Plague in Strasbourg, France, when hundreds of people danced continuously for days.

ECHOES (@tanzkabuff  @rekambergerak @theloniousmusic ) membuka kemungkinan itu lewat pertunjukan interdisipliner yang mempertemukan tubuh, teknologi, ritual, dan suara untuk menggambarkan kontras dalam kondisi masyarakat di tengah percepatan teknologi masa kini.🌱

Pada spektrum yang berbeda, lanskap bunyi bergeser ke eksplorasi MAHAMBORO (@thisismahamboro ) atas persimpangan antara suara akustik dan sintesis. Di penghujung pertunjukan, GABSAV (@gabsav__ ) menghadirkan synth, sampling, dan vokal mentah yang membentuk atmosfer yang intim sekaligus inovatif.

—
Still in your mind? 🎶 Last night (26/07), sound took many waves on the performa•ARTJOG x Bakti Budaya Djarum Foundation stage.

ECHOES opened that possibility with an interdisciplinary performance bringing together the body, technology, ritual, and sound to illustrate the contrasts in societal conditions amid the acceleration and optimization of technology in contemporary life.

On a different spectrum, MAHAMBORO shifted the experience through an exploration of acoustic and electronic sound. Bringing the performance to a close, GABSAV blended synths, sampling, and raw vocals into an intimate and innovative atmosphere.🎸

#ARTJOG #ARTJOG2026 #ARSLONGA #GENERATIO #performaARTJOG

We are entering Buath Gurru season, a time where native grasses are flowering and insects and butterflies are emerging from their slumber. It’s a time where the swamp frogs have been bonking away at sunset. Many snakes will have sloughed by now — shedding a mass of dead skin, parasites, and excess in order to make way for the unknown possibilities, for growth. Shedding takes time, it is a painful and liberating process all enmeshed together. Rather than waiting for who the snake will become after it sheds, the snake is asking us to remember who we are right now. 

The holiday season is upon us, which can be a lonely time for many of us. We’re creating time and space to be together. We’ll be launching our latest zine, featuring a stunning lineup of queer and trans Asian contributors locally and internationally. Join us for an afternoon of zine readings, music, food, a cute drop-in craft activity and a relaxed space for you to (un)coil in. 🧶

We’re delighted to be invited by Sticky for a month-long residency as part of their Window Gallery space. We’ll be showcasing our zine contributor artworks across all of December.

After 7 years of fundraising and mutual aid for various projects, this year our profits are going back to us so we can support queer and trans Asian artists and writers, our programming and all the production and labour that goes into this publishing project. Thank you so much for supporting us.

Like the snake, we invite you to come as you are. We can’t wait to see you and celebrate our Year of the Snake Zine and 7 years of Red Pocket Press with you all 🐍🍊🍉🌼

A truly beautiful weekend in the park! 💜

Four unforgettable days and nights of stunning festival weather and an atmosphere of togetherness – WOMADelaide 2026 was a celebration of connection and stories of possibility. 

Saturday saw the highest attendance in several years and iconic performances from Yothu Yindi and Grace Jones. Throughout the weekend on Foundation Stage, Baker Boy was a favourite for all ages with sky-high energy, while Oumou Sangaré's divine vocals transported the audience with the sublime serenity of Malian rhythm and song. The stunning choreography of Rosas Danst Rosas mesmerised, while electrifying performances from Orange Blossom, Arrested Development, and Obongjayar had everyone on their feet.

Despite the challenges thrown up in the past week, we found a way to come together and celebrate music and community. A huge thank you to our artists, audience, volunteers, crew and partners for making another instalment of WOMADelaide not just possible, but enjoyable and welcoming for all.

Sticky Institute is extremely excited to present our 2025 City of Literature Virtual Resident Ali Raid!!

Ali Raid was born in Babil, Iraq, in 1998. He is a writer, cultural practitioner and artist. His work explores identity, mental health, heritage, and community storytelling through experimental and participatory forms. He has curated and led more than twenty cultural projects, including Montawi (2023), Iraq’s first mental health–themed zine funded by UNESCO; Creative Roots
(2024–25), a year-long heritage program across three Iraqi cities supported by the J.M. Kaplan Fund; and Paya Paya (2024), an interactive installation on accessibility and freedom of movement displayed in Baghdad.
In 2025, Ali was awarded a CrossCulture Fellowship (ifa/CCP) at the Berlin Art Institute and was selected as Virtual Writer in Residence with Sticky Institute, Melbourne UNESCO City of Literature.

Ali writes poetry, short fiction, and experimental texts, often merging visual and literary forms.

Selected works will be included under agreement, and photographers will retain full copyright and will be credited (or not - up to you 😉)

Karya eksperimental “The Disco of Roots” oleh Jessica Soekidi (@jessicasoekidi ) menantang gagasan tentang identitas baku, memandangnya sebagai konstruksi yang cair. Melalui eksplorasinya terhadap umbi-umbian, karya ini menilik kembali pertumbuhan, reproduksi, dan pembangunan identitas yang terus berlangsung sebagai proses dinamis dan relasional melintasi berbagai geografi, generasi, dan sistem ekologis. 

Yuk, berbincang dengan Jessica Soekidi dalam program Meet The Artist, Kamis, 16 Juli 2026. 🥔 Daftarkan dirimu melalui artjog.id/MTA 

—
The experimental work “The Disco of Roots” by Jessica Soekidi challenges the notion of fixed identity, viewing it instead as a fluid construct. Through her exploration of tubers, the work reexamines growth, reproduction, and the ongoing construction of identity as dynamic, relational processes across geographies, generations, and ecological systems.

Join us for a conversation with Jessica Soekidi on Meet The Artist, Thursday, 16  July  2026. 🍠 Register at artjog.id/MTA

—
Mira Rizki presents a series of material witnesses to citizens’ feelings of powerlessness amid societal disillusionment. Drawing from 21 recordings through interviews with close associates and anonymous participants, revealing fears, frustrations, and anxieties about the future, especially coming from her generation. An archive of collective concerns urging audiences to listen beyond words and recognize the silent voices embedded in material form.🔊

Inspired by the orchid’s specific and adaptive ways of growing, the work by Eldine Syifa reflects on the experience of growing within rigid systems. Through the forms of metal orchids, she explores the impulse of play as a method, an active way, and a strategy to negotiate, maintain one’s own identity, and create space for intuition and change.💐

🏕️ Un camping que cuida, conserva y comparte 💚

El camping también forma parte de la sostenibilidad de Bilbao BBK Live.

Por eso, este año impulsamos de nuevo el Programa de Recogida Solidaria en el Camping, una iniciativa para reducir residuos, fomentar un consumo más consciente y facilitar una segunda vida a materiales de acampada que estén en buen estado.
Ayúdanos a tener un camping más verde y responsable:

🌱 Trae solo lo necesario.
🤝 Cuida tus enseres durante la estancia.
♻️ Repara o recicla lo que se estropee.
🏕️ Llévate de vuelta todo lo que puedas volver a utilizar.
💚 Si deseas donar, que sean solo materiales en buen estado.

El domingo 12 de julio, durante la salida del camping, el equipo BALORE a la entrada/salida recogerá, revisará y clasificará tiendas, sacos, esterillas, sillas, mesas, colchones inflables y otros materiales útiles de acampada.

Los materiales en buen estado se entregarán a entidades sociales del territorio: Euskalerriko Eskautak Bizkaia, Errefuxiatuak Bizkaia / Ongi Etorri Errefuxiatuak Bizkaia — OEEB y KOOP SF34.

Porque cuidar el festival también es cuidar el espacio que compartimos.

Mais uma convenção passou. Mais um ano. Mais uma história para guardar na memória. Estes três dias são difíceis de explicar a quem está de fora. São intensos, caóticos, cansativos… mas ao mesmo tempo são das experiências mais bonitas que posso viver. São três dias que parecem uma verdadeira montanha-russa de emoções. Há nervosismo, adrenalina, dúvidas, superação… e no meio de tudo isso há uma sensação muito forte: a de estar exatamente onde devo estar. Durante estes três dias sinto-me viva. Sinto que tudo aquilo que comecei a amar quando ainda era apenas um sonho ou um desenho num papel faz realmente sentido. É nestes momentos que tenho a certeza de que escolhi o caminho certo. Que é isto que eu amo fazer. É o terceiro ano que participo e com o passar do tempo, vou percebendo cada vez mais uma coisa importante: a verdadeira competição não é com os outros artistas. Nunca foi. A maior competição é connosco próprios. São três dias a lutar contra as nossas próprias inseguranças. Contra aqueles pensamentos que aparecem no silêncio da nossa cabeça e que às vezes tentam convencer-nos de que não somos capazes. É uma batalha constante contra o medo de falhar, contra a pressão do tempo que parece sempre correr mais depressa do que nós, contra aquela voz interior que insiste em dizer que talvez não vá dar. Mas depois dá e quando finalmente termina, quando olhamos para o trabalho feito, para cada detalhe, para cada linha, para cada hora de dedicação, percebemos uma coisa muito simples: demos tudo o que tínhamos. E nesse momento nasce um orgulho silencioso, daqueles que não precisam de muito barulho, porque sabemos que fizemos algo especial. Quero também deixar um agradecimento muito especial à minha amiga Liliana, que mais um ano aceitou este desafio comigo de coração aberto. Agarrou esta proposta com unhas e dentes e levou-a até ao fim com uma força incrível. E por fim, quero agradecer a todos os que fazem parte deste caminho: à minha família, amigos, clientes e a todas as pessoas que passaram pelo nosso stand para dar uma força ! Agora é respirar fundo, guardar tudo o que estes dias me ensinaram e continuar a crescer. Que venha a próxima ✨

Di antara rimbunnya dedaunan Leuweung Salira, Intan Anggita Pratiwie (@intananggitapratiwie ) menghadirkan simulasi hutan suci yang berakar pada pengetahuan spiritual Sunda dan konservasi alam. Di pusatnya terdapat Air Pertiwi yang melambangkan air purba sebagai sumber kehidupan. Diiringi komposisi musik pemulihan, karya instalasi ini mengajak pengunjung untuk melakukan rekoneksi dengan diri dan alam. 🍃

Tidak hanya menghadirkan karya instalasi dari tekstil daur ulang, Intan juga memberikan pengalaman menikmati karyanya melalui alunan musik dan pembacaan serat Sewaka Dharma, yang berkolaborasi dengan Fariz Alwan (@fariz.always ) dan Keshia Aita (@_klav_ ), di panggung performa•ARTJOG x Bakti Budaya Djarum Foundation pada Senin (06/07).

—
Amid the dense foliage of Leuweung Salira, Intan Anggita Pratiwie envisioned a sacred and protected forest inspired by Sundanese spiritual knowledge and the preservation of nature. At its center lies Air Pertiwi, representing primordial water and life itself. Featuring a sound-healing composition, this installation invites the audience to reconnect with themselves and with nature. 🪷

In addition to presenting an installation made from recycled textiles, Intan also offered an experience of enjoying her work through music and a reading from the Sewaka Dharma text, in collaboration with Fariz Alwan and Keshia Aita, on the performa•ARTJOG x Bakti Budaya Djarum Foundation stage on Monday (06/07).

🌱 Intan Anggita Pratiwie, Leuweung Salira, 2026.

Among the most secret sounds on the planet, the music of the Bhutan Balladeers is classical music from the Buddhist kingdom of Bhutan 🪷

Their Zhungdra music dates back to the dawn of the 17th century and features extended vocal tones that weave complex patterns and melodies, supported by minimal instrumental, usually just double-stringed lutes, wooden flutes and two-stringed fiddles. The performers sing in the Choekey language, indecipherable even to the majority of Bhutanese, except the Buddhist monks. 

The Bhutan Balladeers’ debut album was recorded in a hilltop forest outside of the capital, Thimphu and released by Glitterbeat Records in 2024. That same summer, a touring trio from the group became the first Bhutanese artists to perform at the WOMAD festival in the UK – don't miss their debut at #WOMADelaide! Performing Saturday and Monday at the festival.

Based in Iranian folk traditions yet shaped by the rich musical sounds of Tehran in the 60s and 70s, Ashkan Shafiei’s music blends nostalgia and innovation in ways that defy definition. 

Raised in Iran on smuggled pre-revolution cassette tapes and later influenced by Western genres via the internet, Ashkan’s influences reflect a life lived between worlds. He plays the rubab, the national instrument of Afghanistan, which was gifted to him before he moved to Sydney. The singer, songwriter, multi-instrumentalist and composer approaches music as an extension of identity – a deeply personal exploration of memory, belonging, and transformation, expressed through poetic metaphors, hypnotic rhythms, and soulful melodies.

Performing with a full band on Friday 6 and Sunday 8 March, plus take a seat at Taste The World on Saturday evening for an authentic Iranian recipe cooked by Ashkan.

A music and human rights project, Daughters of Donbas — ‘Songs of Stolen Children’ exists to highlight the plight of at least 20,000 Ukranian children abducted from occupied Ukraine and taken to Russia. 

Singer, musician, human rights advocate and war correspondent, Marichka is the powerful voice of the project, in which she performs with a string quartet. Drawing on Ukrainian folk music, Marichka uses the traditional technique of ‘white voice’, characterised by its bright, loud and clear sound, produced with an open throat.

Take a seat for two mesmerising shows on Saturday and Sunday of the festival. Presented with the support of the Government of Canada.

Melalui karya ini, Oberlan Luna (@oberlanluna ) mempertanyakan masa depan manusia ketika keberlangsungan dianggap lebih penting daripada pemulihan. Hidup pun direduksi menjadi fungsi yang harus aktif terus-menerus.🩺

Oberlan Luna merupakan salah satu dari tiga seniman yang menerima Young Artist Award tahun ini. 

—
Upon entering the maze-like installation composed of IV bottles, tubing, and fluids with a suspension system, we imagine the body within a structural dependency, operating without the opportunity to question its ultimate purpose. Through his artwork, Oberlan Luna questions the future of humanity when continuity is valued more highly than recovery, and when life is reduced to a function that must remain perpetually active.💉

Oberlan Luna is one among three artists to receive this year’s Young Artist Award.

🚑 Oberlan Luna, Your Recovery Is Not Required, 2026.
