Pengalaman ruang berisi patung yang imersif oleh Roby Dwi Antono mengeksplorasi generasi, perubahan, dan siklus kehidupan. Melalui figur-figur alien, ia merefleksikan luka yang diwariskan dari generasi ke generasi dengan memasuki rahim, ruang yang begitu personal. Patung berkepala tiga, yang bertengger di genangan air, mewakili berbagai tahapan kehidupan—masa kanak-kanak, dewasa, penuaan, kematian, dan kelahiran kembali. 🌫️

Karya ini merupakan hasil kerja sama dengan Museum of Toys (@museumoftoys ).

—
Roby Dwi Antono’s immersive sculptural and spatial experience explores generation, change, and the cycle of life. Through alien figures, he reflects on inherited generational wounds by entering the womb, signifying a deeply personal space. The three-headed sculpture, perched in a puddle, represents different stages of life—childhood, adulthood, aging, death, and rebirth. 🌬️

This work was created in collaboration with Museum of Toys.

Ingatan🧠 masyarakat👫 dan materialitas🔩 dalam seni kontemporer menjadi tema dalam presentasi karya @galeriruangdini , melalui dialog antara pendirinya, Andy Dewantoro, dan dua senimannya, Krishnamurti Suparka dan Carla Agustian.

@andydewantoro membangkitkan ingatan yang memudar melalui hamparan sinematik yang dipenuhi bayangan, rumah terbengkalai, reruntuhan, dan lingkungan sekitarnya. Kemudian, @betweentheinbetween mendorong kita untuk mempertimbangkan berbagai bentuk batas lewat eksplorasi struktur masyarakat, budaya digital, dan ruang perkotaan. Sementara itu, @carlaagustian mengangkat tekstur dan jejak dari objek sehari-hari serta ruang domestik yang menjadi saksi bisu kehidupan. 

Cari tahu lebih lanjut tentang karya para seniman di artjog.id 

—
Memory, society, and materiality within the contemporary art landscape become the theme in the work by Ruang Dini in a dialogue between its founder, Andy Dewantoro, and two of its artists, Krishnamurti Suparka and Carla Agustian.

Andy Dewantoro presents cinematic landscapes steeped in shadows-abandoned structures, ruins, and environments evoking fading memories. Furthermore, Krishnamurti Suparka probes how these frameworks shape identity and space through exploration of themes like societal structures, urban landscapes, and digital culture. Additionally, Carla Agustian captures the textures and traces of everyday objects and domestic spaces, which serve as silent witnesses to life.

Visit artjog.id for more details about the story behind the artworks.

A collage of dark pop, heavily entwined with the avant-garde, Georgia Knight’s music weaves moody, trip-hop pulses with sweeping synth layers, signalling a striking sonic shift from her folk origins 💫

Primarily composing and performing her songs on an autoharp, the singer, songwriter and musician’s stage presence is as memorable as her voice is otherworldly. Since the release of her 2023 EP, she has risen in profile, performing standout festival shows and playing alongside acts like Blonde Redhead (USA), Mogwai (SCT), Angie McMahon and more.

Catch her only WOMADelaide performance on Monday 9 March.

Named by Rolling Stone in their ‘NZ Ones To Watch’, MĀ has continued to go from strength to strength since releasing her self-produced debut album in 2021 🎤

Somewhere between a singer, rapper, spoken word poet, beatmaker, producer and bandleader, MĀ has won over audiences with her distinct blend of abstract downtempo rap, DIY neo-soul and lush ambient music. Born from grief, self-love and an attentive awareness of the natural world, her songs value Māori concepts such as te taiao (the natural world), whakapapa (ancestry), manaakitanga (kindness), as well as humour and emotional honesty.

Performing Saturday 7 and Monday 9 March, plus a workshop on Sunday afternoon at #WOMADelaide.

Stan's Café return to #WOMADelaide with thought-provoking work and teasing commentary 🍚

Founded in 1991 and based in Birmingham, Stan’s Cafe is one of the UK’s foremost independent theatre companies, bringing two performance pieces to WOMADelaide: Of All The People In All The World and The Commentators.

For the beautifully simple installation Of All The People In All The World, Stan’s Cafe converts human population statistics into a landscape of labelled rice piles where one grain = one person. In this way, abstract numbers become easy to understand and gain a powerful emotional force.

Once stalwarts of the radio, whose voices brought major sporting events into the nation's living rooms, these commentators have fallen from favour. Now they bring their unquenchable enthusiasm to commentate on everything and anything except professional sport. Look out and listen out for The Commentators as they roam the festival site and share live and exclusive coverage.

Lewis Major Projects’ Triptych REDUX enters The Studio at #WOMADelaide 👯

Describing himself as “a dance artist with a background in sheep shearing and a foreground in contemporary dance theatre”, Lewis Major didn’t set foot in a theatre until his teens, but has since worked with some of the biggest names in international contemporary dance. His company, Lewis Major Projects, is based in South Australia, where Major grew up on a sheep farm. Triptych REDUX is a reworking of his earlier work Triptych, which the Edinburgh Festival described as “life-changingly beautiful”.

The Studio is located on the ground floor – adjacent the Frome Park Pavilion – under the Upper Plaza where the Taste The World sessions are presented, and is supported by Adelaide Botanic High School students.

Morocco’s first female Gnawa musician, Asmâa Hamzaoui is a leading player in a new wave of women now performing this traditionally male-only brand of evangelistic desert blues 🪕

With her all-female ensemble Bnat Timbouktou she creates a soundscape of rhythmic percussion with her expressive voice and masterfully played guembri (a plucked lute) at the heart of the performance. Although a traditionalist in her music, Hamzaoui is also a trailblazer, taking Gnawa to places such as the Roskilde Festival in Denmark, BAM in Barcelona and Kaustinen in Finland to keep it alive.

Catch Asmâa Hamzaoui & Bnat Timbouktou Sunday and Monday at #WOMADelaide.

It’s impossible not to smile – and move – watching trumpet master Džambo Agušev and his orchestra performing their spirited style of Macedonian folk 🎺

Playing a fusion of traditional Balkan, Gypsy and Turkish music influenced by swing, jazz, pop and film music, the Džambo Aguševi Orchestra is one of the Balkans’ top brass bands. From humble beginnings in the small Macedonian city of Strumica to conquering stages across the globe, the Džambo Aguševi Orchestra’s extraordinary musical skill and unstoppable energy bring the party.

Weaving together alternative R&B, neo-soul and psychedelic influences, SAN DRAGAN invites audiences into an immersive world where soul meets experimentation and authenticity burns bright 💫

With emotionally raw storytelling, bold lyricism and lush vocals, SAN DRAGAN draws from her personal experiences of overcoming adversity and reclaiming identity. A Burmese-Chinese Australian artist based on Kaurna Land, she made her break into the music scene performing on The Academy Stage as part of the WOMADelaide x NSS Academy in 2025.

Having taken their name from a line in the film 'Hooray For Hollywood', it’s not surprising that there is a cinematic quality to Any Young Mechanic’s music. Formerly known as Wake in Fright, the band incorporates intricate scenes, enthralling narratives and unique characters into its lyrics, with a spectrum of moods and emotions stretching through the music.

In 2024, the Adelaide-based five-piece won the Helpmann Academy’s Creative Innovator program to help fund an Australian and international publicity campaign for the release of their 2026 debut album 'The Modern Shoe Is Ruining the Foot'.

Five Things With is a quick-fire format built around five prompts. A way to move past the usual interview answers and hopefully get to something more real, instinctive and unexpected.

Kicking things off with @nilsleonard felt like the only right way to start.

He probably doesn’t need an introduction, but for those of you living slightly outside the advertising bubble: Nils is the co-founder of @uncommon.creative.studio , arguably the hottest creative company in advertising right now, sitting somewhere between advertising, branding, culture and contemporary art.

In the last few years they’ve made some of the industry’s most talked-about work, launched products, opened new offices, built a cult-like reputation and somehow ended up exhibiting at the Venice Biennale too.

Beyond the work itself, what I’ve always found inspiring about him is the clarity of thought, the ambition and the ability to make creativity feel bigger than just “making campaigns”.

Genuinely grateful to @offfest and Zoe for the chance to spend 15 minutes with a talent and personality like his.

Spearheaded by Melbourne-born, Berlin-based drummer and producer Ziggy Zeitgeist, Zeitgeist Freedom Energy Exchange brings together influences of jazz, funk and electronic dance music to create a signature ‘hi-tech jazz’ 🎷

One of the coolest acts on the club circuit, Z*F*E*X have performed at Church of Sound and We Out Here Festival in the UK, ÜBERJAZZ Festival in Hamburg, Meredith Music Festival and Melt Festival in Australia, just to mention a few. 

Their 2025 release ‘Inspire // Radicalise’ brings their dance-floor energy to jazz improvisations, while tapping into a late 70s/early 80s production era – hear it performed on Friday 6 March at #WOMADelaide.

Young trailblazers of an ancient art form, Xylourides are the youth brigade of Cretan folk music 🇬🇷

Descendants of legendary musicians George Xylouris and Psarantonis, and hailing from the epicentre of the movement in Anogeia in the mountains of Crete, twins Adonis and Nikos and their sister Apollonia Xylouris are not just caretakers of this folk music, they are perhaps its finest working exponents. The group has made the music their own, infusing it with a hyper energy and youthful enthusiasm that is infectious and powerful, while honouring all the strict traditions carried through generations.

Catch two performances from the young Greek musicians on Friday and Sunday of the festival, plus a Taste The World appearance on Saturday afternoon.

Megatronic hits the decks on Sunday 8 March at #WOMADelaide 🎧

With a career spanning over two decades, UK-born Megane Quashie — who now lives between Dubai and Lisbon — has transcended borders and established herself as a maverick force on the global music scene. Megatronic’s infectious energy and distinct voice have found their way onto house labels such as Razor-N-Tape, Freerange, Feedasoul, and The Remedy Project, with her songwriting and vocals elevating dancefloors worldwide. 

Her sets are a masterclass in fluidity, gliding across electronic, African and Arabic rhythms with an effortless command of groove.

The SoccerActress blends storytelling, comedy and movement with seriously impressive keep up skills.

As the story unfolds, the juggling becomes part of the journey, guiding you through a performance that feels like a road movie brought to life. Charming, physical and quietly powerful, it’s a show about courage, determination and finding your footing.

Things to do during OFFF: Paramnésico by @desilence_ at @load.gallery !

For over two decades, Barcelona-based artist duo Desilence has expanded the possibilities of live visuals, positioning themselves among the pioneers of visual scenography. But what does visual scenography mean in their practice?

Tatiana Halbach explains that it emerged from a desire to take the visual beyond the screen and adapt it to the surrounding space — whether a theatre, an architectural structure, a sculpture, or even a restaurant. It allowed them to treat visuals not as images contained within a surface, but as scenography itself. Regardless of scale, they have consistently sought to move beyond the screen’s confinement, only to return to the nine screens of Load gallery for their solo show, which draws on a months-long dream-recording experiment.

🗓️ April 16-18, 16:00-20:00 at @load.gallery

For more than two decades, @offfest Barcelona has established itself as one of the leading international gatherings dedicated to creativity, design and visual culture. What began as a pioneering initiative to bring together designers, digital artists and visual creators has evolved into a global platform where disciplines, ideas and new ways of understanding contemporary creativity intersect.

In its upcoming edition, the festival will once again bring together in Barcelona some of the most influential voices on the international creative scene, alongside a new generation of talent redefining the visual language of our time.

As media partners, we recently spoke with @pepsalazar, co-founder of OFFF, about the spirit of the festival, the relationship between creativity, technology and the city, and Barcelona’s role as one of the world’s great creative hubs. 

ES

Durante más de dos décadas, @offfest Barcelona se ha consolidado como uno de los encuentros internacionales de referencia dedicados a la creatividad, el diseño y la cultura visual. Lo que comenzó como una iniciativa pionera para reunir a diseñadores, artistas digitales y creadores visuales ha evolucionado hasta convertirse en una plataforma global donde confluyen disciplinas, ideas y nuevas formas de entender la creatividad contemporánea.

En su próxima edición, el festival volverá a reunir en Barcelona a algunas de las voces más influyentes de la escena creativa internacional, junto a una nueva generación de talento que está redefiniendo el lenguaje visual de nuestro tiempo.

One of Melbourne’s most highly regarded physical theatre ensembles, Born in a Taxi (BIAT) mix dance with humour, the profound with the profane, and the familiar with the unlikely, to produce highly original, physically driven and participatory works 🎭

The company’s diverse performance backgrounds and ensemble movement improvisation create a performance style that lives somewhere between the cracks of theatre and dance. Weaving through the crowds during the festival, you'll find BIAT changing costumes through five roving performances: Higher Order, Illuminati, Please Wait Here, Zebras and The Sleep Keepers.

Family band Annie & The Caldwells make their WOMADelaide debut in March ✨

Annie Caldwell, her husband, two daughters, two sons, and goddaughter make powerful disco-soul-gospel music together. Hailing from West Point, Mississippi, Annie started the band when her daughter began singing the blues instead of the church music she had grown up with. More than 20 years of music-making later, in 2025, the band released their debut album ‘Can’t Lose My (Soul)’, which The Guardian describes as “a fantastic album – funky, gritty and powerful, packed with incredible singing and potent songs that cast a stark eye over life’s hardships”. 

Their real-life troubles and experiences are at the centre of their music, which infuses spirituality and gospel with grit and street savvy – witness the power of family on Sunday and Monday at the festival.

In 2026, all WOMADelaide stages will be powered using 100% renewable energy – setting a new benchmark for the festival by becoming South Australia’s first festival to power the majority of its event with renewables! 🌱

This year the festival will use renewable energy as the primary source of electricity, with the majority of liquid fuel being 100% renewable. This is achieved through a mix of B100 fuel – a biodiesel made entirely from organic matter and trialled at the festival since 2021 – and the latest addition, HVO fuel.

"Sustainability is something we’re all really passionate about, and we’ve been working hard to reduce and offset the festival’s carbon emissions while minimising our environmental impact" – Festival Director Ian Scobie AM.

Pioneers of the traditional music of the Gogo (or Wagogo) people, The Zawose Queens will perform their dance-inspired, female-led music on Saturday 7 and Monday 9 March at #WOMADelaide 🦁 

In their native Kigogo language, their lyrics tell of a passion for music and the wonders of life, and speak of pride in their environment, in tradition and in their East African roots. The late Dr Hukwe Zawose, who performed at WOMADelaide in 1995, is the father of Pendo Zawose and grandfather of Leah Zawose, the aunt and niece duo behind The Zawose Queens. These next generations of women are now telling their own stories in their own voices.

One night, two big Fringe hits: London Calling and MARVELous made for the ultimate double feature.

London Calling is a high-energy fusion of circus, magic, comedy and cabaret, hosted by the brilliantly witty Paul Dabek. Expect jaw-dropping aerials, hypnotic hula hooping, elite juggling and all-star performers fresh from Cirque du Soleil, La Clique and The Illusionists.

MARVELous delivers outrageous parody with aerials, live vocals, dance and a risqué edge. Think Marvel heroes collide with Dirty Dancing, Magic Mike and The Greatest Showman — with Deadpool leading the chaos for a laugh-out-loud, unapologetically cheeky night.

Both shows are closing this weekend — and trust us, these are the kind of Fringe acts that sell out fast.

💼 JUST BUSINESS @ Fringe World Perth

Fringe moments where you walk in thinking, 'Okay… acrobatics and juggling — let’s see,'
and walk out genuinely blown away.

Because WOW.

We were front row, centre — and let me tell you… this show does not hold back.

@duovann's Just Business isn’t just circus.
It’s flirtation in motion.
It’s strength meeting elegance.
It’s cheeky humour colliding with jaw-dropping skill.
It’s dance, acrobatics, wheel artistry and chemistry so electric you feel it in your chest.

Went in for a fun night out with a bestie.
Left buzzing.

Fast-paced.
Awe-inspiring.
Full of sizzles and giggles.

Impressive, cheeky and genuinely funny — jaw-dropping tricks with Dirty Dancing energy — powerful, playful and full of chemistry.

And yes… I got pulled up on stage (absolutely not my usual thing 😅) — but somehow even that became part of the fun.

The juggling? Hands down the best I’ve ever seen.
The ballroom dancing? A surprise highlight.
The music + video backdrop? Set the tone from the very first beat.
The performers? World-class, playful and SO present with the audience.

It’s bold. It’s clever. It’s sexy-fun.
They tease. They compete. They flirt. They fly.
And somehow… it all works.

📍 The Royale Theatre at @planetroyaleperth
